courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Financial Accounting
courses.description: Accounting concepts and techniques essential to the administration of a business enterprise: analyzing and recording financial transactions; accounting valuation and allocation practices; preparation, analysis and interpretation of financial statements; international accounting issues.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Managerial Accounting
courses.description: Introduction to managerial accounting; product costing; budgetary control and responsibility accounting; analysis and techniques for aiding management planning and control decisions; basic income tax concepts for planning business transactions.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Intermediate Accounting
courses.description: Accounting theory; preparation of income statements, balance sheets, and statements of cash flows and comprehensive income; IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards); present value concepts; assets, revenue recognition and investments.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Intermediate Accounting
courses.description: Accounting theory; IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards); present value concepts; liabilities and stockholders' equity; pensions; leases; earnings per share; financial statement analysis; accounting changes and error analysis; accounting for income taxes and statement of cash flows.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Cost Accounting
courses.description: Accounting information for management of manufacturing and service enterprises; cost records; cost behavior and allocation; product costing and inventory valuation; flexible budgeting; standard costs; responsibility accounting; cost planning and control; and operating decision analysis.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Accounting Information Systems
courses.description: Organization and implementation of information technology for the collection, organization and presentation of accounting information with an emphasis on enterprise resource planning systems.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Concepts of Federal Income Tax Accounting
courses.description: Federal tax system, federal income taxation relating to federal tax system, federal income taxation relating to individuals, corporations, partnerships and fiduciaries. Federal estate and gift taxes.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Advanced Accounting
courses.description: Business combinations; meaning, usefulness and methodology of consolidated financial statements; investments and additional advanced topics; consolidated financial statements for overseas units of U.S.-based multinational companies; translations of foreign currencies, derivatives.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Auditing
courses.description: Auditing standards and procedures used by financial and operational auditors. Management information and computer systems, internal control, audit evidence, professional responsibilities and legal liabilities, standards of reporting financial information.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Accounting for Governmental and Nonprofit Entities
courses.description: Fund accounting as applied to governmental and nonprofit entities; state and federal governments, municipalities, hospitals and universities. Budgets, tax levies, revenues and appropriations, expenditures and encumbrances, various types of funds and accounting statements.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Emerging Technologies in Accounting
courses.description: Learning and applying (in the field of accounting) technologies that will become a cornerstone for success, such as Robotic Process Automation using UIPath, as well as data extraction using Microsoft Power Query.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Forensic Accounting and Fraud Examination
courses.description: Methods to prevent and detect fraud. Current cases dealing with accounting fraud and appropriate methods to prevent or detect fraudulent behavior.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Accounting Data Analytics
courses.description: Data analytics as it pertains to accounting professionals. Three major areas that comprise analytics are Data Reporting, Data Visualization and Predictive Analytics. Uses emerging technology to show the practice of data analytics in the real world.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Taxation of Business Entities
courses.description: Additional tax knowledge on tax research, corporate taxation, partnership taxation, S Corps, transfer taxation, gift taxes and accounting for income tax. Other topics, such as SALT, may be included.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Internal Audit and Control
courses.description: Professional standards and procedures used by internal auditors. Planning, performing, communicating risk based assurance and consulting engagements. Advanced topics in control; governance, risk management, fraud and information technology. Requires departmental permission for non-Accounting undergraduate majors and all graduate students.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Seminar in Financial Statement Analysis
courses.description: Analysis of demand and supply forces underlying the provision of financial statements; distributional, cross-sectional and time series properties of financial statement numbers; financial decision-making processes and the uses of financial statement information for decision making.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Financial Controls for Entrepreneurs
courses.description: Tools and frameworks to manage the financial aspects of small to medium businesses. Topics include cash flows, budgeting, internal controls, performance metrics, valuation, funding sources, corporate forms and legal regulations. May include casework, research and fieldwork with selected local businesses. No credit toward the following: B.A. Business Administration, Accounting concentration; M.S. Accountancy; M.S. Taxation.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: Planned and supervised internship experience. Requires that: student obtains an internship; internship site and position meet CICE approval; consent of academic department. Letter grade or credit/no credit options available. Only 3-unit letter grade option will fulfill practicum requirement. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Accounting Theory and Professional Research
courses.description: Provides an analytical framework for managerial decision-making using accounting information. Explore solutions to professional accounting problems by researching the FASB Codification.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Seminar in Accounting Data Analytics
courses.description: Introduction to data extraction, analytic and data visualization tools used in business today, and techniques for Big Data analyses. Hands-on experience with several key tools used to transform raw data into actionable knowledge.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Advanced Auditing and Analytics
courses.description: Auditing theory and practices; professional ethics; auditing standards; Securities and Exchange Commission and stock exchange regulations; auditor's legal liability; statement trends and techniques.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Seminar in Professional Accounting Communications
courses.description: Compilation and composition of accounting reports and client presentations relating to accountants' working papers, client engagement letters, management advisory reports and prospectuses.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Seminar in Accounting Information Systems
courses.description: Case studies of computer-based accounting systems used by organizations such as universities, banks, industrial corporations and CPA firms. Accounting information, reports, and internal controls.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Financial Accounting
courses.description: Accumulation, organization and interpretation of financial and quantitative data relevant to the activities of corporate business enterprises; analysis of financial reports; current regulatory reporting requirements with attention to business ethics and an understanding of global reporting issues.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Corporate Governance and External Reporting
courses.description: Institutional knowledge on internal and external corporate governance mechanisms and the SEC regulation of financial reporting. How to prepare SEC filings and learn about how corporate governance influences firm performance.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Tax Research, Practice and Procedures
courses.description: Methodology of tax research, including case studies; the management of a tax practice; administration procedures governing tax controversies; rights and obligations of taxpayers and tax practitioners. Requires basic knowledge of US Federal Income Tax.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Seminar in Taxation of Property and M&A Transactions
courses.description: Concepts, rules and issues with regard to the taxation of transactions involving different types of property. Taxation of property transactions when a buyer acquires another company.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Seminar in Taxation of Employee Compensation
courses.description: Federal taxation relating to employee compensation including pensions and profit sharing, stock options, ESOPs, IRAs, Keoghs, maximum tax 5-year averaging, death benefits, group term life, etc.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Seminar in Taxation of Flow-Through Entities
courses.description: Federal taxation relating to partnerships, estates, trusts and other special entities.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Accounting Capstone - Advances in Academic Research and Technologies
courses.description: Culminating intellectual experience to use knowledge learned. Solve complex accounting problems using analytic tools applied to real world data with guidance from faculty and professionals.

courses.subject: AFAM
courses.title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
courses.description: Perspectives through which people of color have come to see themselves in terms of their own heroes, cultures and contributions to the societies in which they live and the world in general. (AFAM 101, ASAM 101, and CHIC 101 are the same course)

courses.subject: AFAM
courses.title: Critical Race Theory
courses.description: How race, sexuality, ethnicity, gender, disability and class influence the law, using a critical race theory lens. An extension of Critical Legal Theory, formed in the 1980s, to explore how racism and structural inequality are institutionalized within the legal system.

courses.subject: AFAM
courses.title: Introduction to Black Creative Expression
courses.description: Introduction to Black originators and innovators of art forms, such as performing, literary and visual. Critical responses to art forms in both historical and contemporary contexts. Understand trends in creativity and imagination that cross expressive forms in Black communities.

courses.subject: AFAM
courses.title: Survey of American History with Emphasis on Ethnic Minorities
geCategories:
American History, Institutions & Values
Free Course Material
courses.description: Survey of American history from prehistoric times (before 1492) to the present with special emphasis on the role of race and ethnicity. (HIST 190, AFAM 190, ASAM 190 and CHIC 190 are the same course.)

courses.subject: AFAM
courses.title: Black Lives Matter Creative and Critical Ideas
courses.description: Black Lives Matter movement origins, controversies and legacies. Creative and critical responses to social activism in communities of color. Engaging critical debates around over-policing, anti-black racism and bias.

courses.subject: AFAM
courses.title: African American Music Appreciation
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Black music in America; the sociological conditions that help produce various forms of black music. (AFAM 356 and MUS 356 are the same course)

courses.subject: AFAM
courses.title: Development of African American Children and Youth
courses.description: Understanding cognitive and socio-emotional development of African American children and youth is facilitated through comprehensive examinations of significant African and African American cultural and historical experiences. (CAS 370 and AFAM 370 are the same course.)

courses.subject: AFAM
courses.title: Hip Hop Culture
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Origins and influences of hip hop on culture, fashion, movies, television, advertising, attitude, music, dancing and slang among African Americans. Impact of the hip hop culture phenomenon on American and global societies.

courses.subject: AFAM
courses.title: Language and Power in African American Culture
courses.description: Language use within the African American community. Topics include language history, dialect vs. language, communicative practices, language in education policy, language and ideology, and language attitudes. (ENGL 410 and AFAM 410 are the same course.)

courses.subject: AGNG
courses.title: Introduction to Aging Studies
courses.description: Multidisciplinary overview of: characteristics, strengths and problems of older persons; diversity in aging process involving gender, race, ethnicity, subculture; services to older adults; gerontology as an academic discipline and a field of practice. (AGNG 133, SOCI 133, PUBH 133, HUSR 133 and PSYC 133 are the same course.)

courses.subject: AGNG
courses.title: California Gold: Diversity and Aging
courses.description: California serves as a microcosm for studying diversity and aging. Course considers race/ethnicity, gender, disability, income, sexual orientation and religion among aging Californians. Highlights discrimination, racism and current/future needs and support services in the context of current events.

courses.subject: AGNG
courses.title: Advanced Writing with a Focus on Aging
courses.description: Academic intensive writing in an aging studies context. Read, think, write and revise using current aging text and journal articles in written and oral formats. Assignments involve organizing complex ideas, with feedback provided throughout the course for revision.

courses.subject: AGNG
courses.title: Aging and Dementia
courses.description: Physiological, psychological, social, economic aspects of dementia; its impact on the individual, family and society, with an emphasis on Alzheimer's disease.

courses.subject: AGNG
courses.title: Gerontology Undergraduate Internship
courses.description: Integration of professional and academic experience through internships with external employers (120-150 hours of fieldwork). Supervised experience in organizations that serve older adults and their families, and written reflections on these experiences. Prerequisites: Consent of instructor and Program Coordinator. Requires consent of instructor and Program Coordinator.

courses.subject: AGNG
courses.title: Biopsychosocial Perspectives in Aging
courses.description: Biological, psychological and social concepts of aging upon which professional practice in gerontology is based.

courses.subject: AGNG
courses.title: Public Organizational Theory and Behavior
courses.description: Management-oriented analysis of organizational behavior. Treatments of decision-making, leadership, communication, group dynamics and ethical aspects of organization. Applying theories of administration and systems management to public and volunteer programs and services. (POSC 526 and AGNG 526 are the same course).

courses.subject: AGNG
courses.title: Research Methods in Gerontology, Project Development
courses.description: Research processes and problems in gerontology; more detailed study of applied research, including program evaluation in the field of gerontology.Development of a project to conclude in AGNG 594 as a culminating experience.

courses.subject: AGNG
courses.title: Gerontology Internship
courses.description: Supervised experience in organizations that serve older adults and their families. May be repeated once for credit. Requires classified status in M.S. in Gerontology program, and consent of instructor and Program Coordinator.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: Questioning America
geCategories:
Introduction to Social & Behavioral Sci
Free Course Material
courses.description: What is American culture? Introduction to multiple methods used to understand ideas of America and American culture; explore diverse techniques to investigate questions of power, belonging and everyday life.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: Introduction to American Studies
geCategories:
American History, Institutions & Values
Free Course Material
courses.description: With the concept of culture as a unifying principle, focus is on four separate time periods in order to provide the framework for an understanding of American civilization. Several different kinds of documents will be used to illustrate the nature and advantages of an interdisciplinary approach.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: Introduction to American Popular Culture
courses.description: Historical exploration of popular culture in America as it reflects and contributes to the search for meaning in everyday life. Heroes, myths of success, symbols of power, images of romance, consumerism, race and sexual identity.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: American Experiences
courses.description: American identities and beliefs, through a sampling of historical and contemporary voices from different groups of Americans. Similarities and differences in Americans' experiences based on class, race, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, region and other identities.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: American Immigrant Cultures
geCategories:
Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
Free Course Material
courses.description: Investigates American immigrant communities, both historical and contemporary, to better understand how their experiences helped shape the meaning of being American. Explores immigrant cultures through literature, music, film, oral history and photographs using interdisciplinary methods.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: Science and Modern America
geCategories:
Implications & Explorations in Phys/Bio
Free Course Material
courses.description: Interdisciplinary analysis of the relationship between science and culture in the American past and present. Topics include questions of trust, ethics, objectivity, power and identity in developing scientific knowledge in health and medicine, the environment, and technology.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: The American Dream
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Interdisciplinary analysis, in settings both historical and contemporary, of the myth and reality surrounding the notion of America as a land of unparalleled and unlimited possibilities, especially in the achievement of personal material success.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: Seminar in Theory and Method of American Studies
courses.description: Understanding and appreciation of methodology, theories of society and images of humanity as they affect American studies contributions to scholarship. Fulfills the course requirement of the university upper-division baccalaureate writing requirement for American Studies majors.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: California Cultures
courses.description: Who can claim to be Californian? The ideals and realities of what it means to be Californian; investigating how various identities - of race, class, gender, sexuality, region and generation - have interacted in California's cultures, past and present.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: Women, Race, and Ethnicity in American Culture
courses.description: Diversity of women's experiences, including historical and contemporary analysis of groups such as Black American, Asian American, Latina, Arab American and Indigenous women. Course materials include autobiography, fiction, visual and popular arts, and feminist cultural criticism.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: Food and American Culture
courses.description: Food and identities in America from the colonial era to the present, including explorations of American ethnic food,  industrialization of food and contemporary food movements.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: Frontiers and Borderlands in American Culture
courses.description: How ideas about frontiers, borders and "the West" have contributed to American identities and experiences. Topics include popular culture, politics, immigration, gender, racial formation and attitudes toward wilderness.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Supervised research projects in American Studies to be taken with the consent of instructor and department chair. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: AMST
courses.title: Theory and Methods
courses.description: The American Studies movement. Its conceptual and methodological development. The way this development was affected by and in turn reflected larger trends in the culture itself.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Non-Western Cultures and the Western Tradition
courses.description: Changing views of people, nature and culture in Western civilization as related to the impact of non-Western influences, including the use and interpretation of data on non-Western peoples and cultures.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Introduction to Biological Anthropology
courses.description: Humans as biological organisms from an evolutionary perspective. Concepts, methods, findings and issues in the study of the Order primates, including the relationships among fossil monkeys, apes and humans, and the significance of genetic diversity in modern populations.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Introduction to Cultural Anthropology
courses.description: Nature of culture and its significance. Similarities and difference in human cultures. Analyses of family, economy, subsistence, religion, art and other aspects of culture in diverse societies. Central problems of cultural comparison and interpretation.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Introduction to Archaeology
courses.description: Relationship of archaeology, culture history and process, field methods and analysis of archaeological data; uses and abuses of archaeology.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Language and Culture
courses.description: Language in the context of culture. The symbolic nature of language, speech as performance, non-verbal communication, gendered speech and bias in language. Language acquisition, language change and loss, and factors leading to the invention of writing.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Traditional Cultures of the World
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Comparative, worldwide survey of traditional, selected and well-studied ways of life using ethnographic writings and films. Examines diverse ways of life, with an emphasis on small-scale societies.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Anthropology of Religion
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Beliefs and practices in diverse religions, emphasizing cultural context; religion and power; anthropological theories of religion; gods, spirits and spirituality; mythology; religious symbols; rituals and rites of passage; religious specialists; soul and death; magic and witchcraft; and new religious movements. (ANTH 305 and RLST 305 are the same course)

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Psychological Anthropology
courses.description: Relationship of culture to the individual. Child-training in non-western cultures. Survey of concepts, studies and research techniques in psychological anthropology.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Anthropology of Sex and Gender
courses.description: Human sex and gender roles in cross-cultural perspective and the role that gender plays in human social organization. Topics covered include cultural construction of gender; homosexuality, rights of women, evolution and gender. (ANTH 316 and GSS 316 are the same course.)

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Peoples of Native North America
courses.description: Native peoples of North America; origins, languages, culture areas, cultural history; the impact of European contacts.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Peoples of Asia
courses.description: Asian civilizations and cultural traditions: personality configurations in different culture areas; structure of Asian civilizations; and peasant, tribal and ethnic groups of Asia.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Sex, Evolution and Human Nature
courses.description: Evolutionary theory and human evolution; the primate origins of humanity, the evolution of human nature, and the evolutionary foundations of human behavior and cognition.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Museum Science
courses.description: Methods, principles and techniques used in natural history, and small scientific and historical museums. Scope of exhibit and research collections, care and repair of specimens, acquisitions, storage and preparation of presentations in anthropological, historical, biological and paleontological museums.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: The Anthropology of Human Rights
courses.description: Introduction to the study of human rights from anthropological and interdisciplinary perspectives. Examine human rights issues and specific cases of human rights abuses within the context of international and ethno-specific domains.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: The Aztecs and Their Predecessors
courses.description: Archaeological survey of principal Mesoamerica pre-Columbian cultures north and west of the Maya area. Aztecs and their predecessors, religion, art, architecture, intellectual achievements and the Olmec heritage.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Human Evolutionary Anatomy
courses.description: Uses an evolutionary framework to conduct an in-depth and detailed examination of the structure and function of human anatomical systems, their interaction, and their evolutionary histories and how those histories affect health in modern populations.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: History of Anthropology
courses.description: Principal contributions of anthropologists 1850-1950; evolutionary, diffusionist, historical, particularist, configurationalist, and culture and personality approaches in anthropology.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Contemporary Anthropology
courses.description: Anthropologists from 1950 to present; neoevolutionist, sociological, structuralist, psychological and symbolic approaches.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Internship in Anthropology
courses.description: Career opportunities. On-the-job training under faculty supervision in museum, industry or governmental service. One or more papers required. May be repeated once for credit.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Seminar: Selected Topics in Anthropology
courses.description: The chosen topic and a general outline of the seminar are circulated prior to registration. May be repeated for credit with different topic.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Theory and Method in Archaeology
courses.description: Basic theoretical positions and methodological spectrum in archaeological anthropology. Requires instructor permission.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Project
courses.description: Complete a project derived from original field or laboratory research, and/or from library study. Project could also be a museum exhibit, field report or other project. A copy of the approved written component of the project must be filed in the department through the department graduate program adviser. May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 6 units. Requires consent of project adviser.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Fundamental Arabic-A
courses.description: Introduction to essentials of Modern Standard Arabic vocabulary and structures. Basic reading, writing, and conversational skills using culturally appropriate language. Conducted primarily in Arabic.

courses.subject: ARTE
courses.title: Externship in Single Subject Teaching
courses.description: Eight-week practicum (150 hours) fieldwork in single subject classrooms. Credit/No Credit only. A "B" (3.0) or better is required to receive a grade of credit. Students sign up for the appropriate departmental offering. Requires admission to the Single Subject Credential Program. May be repeated once for credit. (EDSC 449E, ARTE 449E, KNES 449E, MAED 449E, MUSE 449E, and THTR 449E are the same course.)

courses.subject: ASAM
courses.title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
courses.description: Perspectives through which people of color have come to see themselves in terms of their own heroes, cultures and contributions to the societies in which they live and the world in general. (AFAM 101, ASAM 101, and CHIC 101 are the same course)

courses.subject: ASAM
courses.title: Survey of American History with Emphasis on Ethnic Minorities
courses.description: Survey of American history from prehistoric times (before 1492) to the present with special emphasis on the role of race and ethnicity. (HIST 190, AFAM 190, ASAM 190 and CHIC 190 are the same course.)

courses.subject: ASAM
courses.title: Ideas, Imagination and Intersections in Ethnic Studies/Asian American Studies
courses.description: Understand contemporary Ethnic Studies/Asian American Studies by examining their roots and agency to imagine a society beyond our nation's historical legacies. Students consider their life experiences through core concepts, research and creative works, and intersectional topics and identities in ES/ASAM.

courses.subject: ASAM
courses.title: Introduction to Multi-Ethnic Literatures of the U.S.
courses.description: Introducing multi-ethnic literatures of the U. S., the course considers texts within their cultural, historical, and socio-political contexts. Relates multi-ethnic literature to the creative and performing arts. Themes covered may include diaspora, migration, memory, history, citizenship, and/or ethnic identities. (CHIC 250, AFAM 250, ASAM 250 and ENGL 250 are the same course.)

courses.subject: ASAM
courses.title: Introduction to Asian Pacific American Studies
courses.description: Interdisciplinary exploration of the experiences of several Asian American groups. Addresses questions of cultural assimilation and cultural persistence, family and gender roles, and literary and popular culture representations.

sections.instructor: Eliza Noh, To Be Announced, To Be Announced, To Be Announced
Eliza Noh, Eliza Noh, Eliza Noh, Eliza Noh

courses.subject: ASAM
courses.title: Asian American Women
courses.description: Interdisciplinary, intersectional examination of Asian Pacific Islander South Asian American women's experiences. Compares and contrasts the APISAA women's experience of social, cultural and political issues in the U.S. and abroad. Engages theoretical analyses and practical applications for empowerment.

courses.subject: ASAM
courses.title: Asian American Foodways
courses.description: Food as a social, cultural and political phenomenon. Topics include colonialism, militarism, labor, protest, refugee resettlement, cultural preservation, cookbooks, memory and identity formation of race, class, gender and sexuality

courses.subject: ASAM
courses.title: Asian Pacific American Cultural Studies
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Asian American life as portrayed through novels, short stories, plays, poetry, film, music, painting, dance and other expressive forms. Examines historical and contemporary works by a variety of Asian and Pacific Americans.

courses.subject: ASAM
courses.title: Asian American Film and Video
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Introduction to major themes in Asian American film and video history and criticism. Asian American aesthetics, history and politics will be examined in areas of film and video direction, production, writing and acting.

courses.subject: ASAM
courses.title: Asian American Psychology
courses.description: Major issues in the Asian American community from a psychosocial perspective, including ethnic identity development, generational conflicts, the "model minority" myth, interracial relationships, attitudes toward mental health services and alternative healing/therapeutic approaches. (ASAM 346 and PSYC 346 are the same course.)

courses.subject: ASAM
courses.title: Internship in Asian American Studies
courses.description: One hundred twenty (120) hours practical experience in some organization serving the Asian Pacific American community. Regular meetings with faculty advisor. May be repeated once for credit. Requires approval of supervising instructor(s).

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Introduction to Astronomy
courses.description: The science of stars, planets, moons and our Sun. Starlight, galaxies and the history of our universe, alien planets and black holes. High school algebra recommended. Co-enrollment in ASTR 101L recommended.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Introduction to Astronomy Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory course investigating the fundamental concepts of astronomy; motion of the night sky, phases of the moon, telescopes, history and composition of the universe, and modern astronomical discoveries.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Applications of Gravitation
courses.description: A physics-first introduction to gravitation, focusing on applications. Spacetime and special relativity. Gravitation as curved spacetime, metrics and geodesics. Applications of gravitation, including black holes, gravitational waves and cosmology.

courses.subject: BUAD
courses.title: Foundations for College Success and Lifelong Learning
courses.description: Knowledge, skills and attitudes necessary to succeed as an undergraduate student. Builds a foundation for life-long learning and creates self-meaning in a global society. Designed for exploring majors, with a focus on longitudinal learning, self-validation and social integration.

sections.instructor: Farifteh Shahbazian, Farifteh Shahbazian, Farifteh Shahbazian, Farifteh Shahbazian, Farifteh Shahbazian, Farifteh Shahbazian, Farifteh Shahbazian, Farifteh Shahbazian, Farifteh Shahbazian

courses.subject: BUAD
courses.title: Business Writing
courses.description: Core communication practices: routing business correspondence, positive, informative, negative and persuasive messages. Introduction to research and job application process.

courses.subject: BUAD
courses.title: Understanding Business
courses.description: Nature, dimensions and forms of business and the role of entrepreneurship in business creation and growth. Development of an understanding of contemporary business issues, including an introduction to major business functions.

courses.subject: BUAD
courses.title: Professional and Career Development
courses.description: Develop and practice skills, conceptual understanding, and self-assessment in interpersonal relationship, critical thinking, diversity management, leadership and team building. Introduce tools and build skills for career exploration and planning.

courses.subject: BUAD
courses.title: Advanced Business Communication
courses.description: Expands knowledge of business communication and develops written and oral communication skills. Study a variety of business cases that understand the function of communication in the modern business world. Analyze real-life business problems and determine when and how to communicate corporate decisions to employees, business partners and the public.

courses.subject: BUAD
courses.title: AI Literacy for Business Students
courses.description: Introduction to artificial intelligence concepts, tools and ethical implications for business professionals. How AI technologies work, evaluate AI-driven business applications and develop frameworks for responsible AI adoption in organizational contexts.

sections.instructor: Matthew Badal, Matthew Badal, Matthew Badal, Matthew Badal, Matthew Badal

courses.subject: BUAD
courses.title: Entertainment Money Management
courses.description: How entertainment, tourism and hospitality firms make money: overview of existing and evolving income generation models in the various industry sectors.

courses.subject: BUAD
courses.title: Starting and Managing a Professional Practice/Small Business
courses.description: Introduces the fundamentals of starting and managing a professional practice or small business. The class targets non-business majors who have an interest in starting their own professional practice or small business after graduation.

courses.subject: BUAD
courses.title: Business Strategy Capstone
courses.description: Tools of strategic management and their application in a business environment. Integrates business functional areas and tools by means of a culminating project. Fulfills the terminal requirement for the MBA degree. Must be taken in the program's final semester during which students can enroll in a maximum of nine units, including a maximum of one core course.

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
courses.description: Perspectives through which people of color have come to see themselves in terms of their own heroes, cultures and contributions to the societies in which they live and the world in general. (AFAM 101, ASAM 101, and CHIC 101 are the same course)

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Communication Skills
courses.description: Basic communication skills, including oral and written expression. A unit on the mechanics of writing and reporting on a term paper is included as part of the course.

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Introduction to Chicano Studies
courses.description: Role of the Chicano in the U.S. The Chicano's cultural values, social organization, urbanization patterns, and the problems in the area of education, politics and legislation.

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Survey of American History with Emphasis on Ethnic Minorities
courses.description: Survey of American history from prehistoric times (before 1492) to the present with special emphasis on the role of race and ethnicity. (HIST 190, AFAM 190, ASAM 190 and CHIC 190 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Chicana and Chicano Environmentalisms
courses.description: Relationships between Chicanx/Latinx communities and environments and ecologies as represented in art, film, literature, oral histories, photography and other forms of cultural production. How Chicanx/Latinx cultural production contributes to understandings about environmentalisms and ecologies.

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Chicana/o Identities
courses.description: Chicana/o identities, from their indigenous beginnings to the present, through categories of gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, national origin and class; surveying interdisciplinary, social scientific, historical and literary sources.

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Introduction to Multi-Ethnic Literatures of the U.S.
courses.description: Introducing multi-ethnic literatures of the U. S., the course considers texts within their cultural, historical, and socio-political contexts. Relates multi-ethnic literature to the creative and performing arts. Themes covered may include diaspora, migration, memory, history, citizenship, and/or ethnic identities. (CHIC 250, AFAM 250, ASAM 250 and ENGL 250 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Music of Mexico
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Historical survey of folk, popular and art music traditions of Mexico and music in Mexican American/Chicano society; pre-Cortesian and contemporary indigenous musical practices; relationship of music to Mexican history and culture. Listening, reading and written work. Intended for non-music majors. May be used as a music-major elective. (MUS 304 and CHIC 304 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Chicana/o Families
courses.description: The Chicana/o family's development as an American social institution focusing on cross-cultural, historical and interdisciplinary perspectives.

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Research and Writing in Ethnic Studies
courses.description: Introduction to research and writing in ethnic studies. Issues of research in ethnic studies (e.g., quantitative v. qualitative analysis, reliability/validity) and specific methods of research (e.g., archives, interviews, oral history). Extensive writing. A "C" (2.0) or better is required to satisfy the upper-division writing requirement.  (ASAM 307, AFAM 307 and CHIC 307 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: La Chicana
courses.description: Cultural influences that the family, religion, economic status and community play upon the lifestyles, values and roles held by Chicanas. (CHIC 313 and GSS 313 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Chicana and Chicano Education
courses.description: Overview of the educational plight of Chicanas/os in the American school system from an interdisciplinary perspective. Addresses educational inequality and social justice phenomenon using various concepts, theories and methodologies.

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: The Chicano Child
courses.description: The Chicano child from preschool through grade six. Emphasizes motor, physical, social, intellectual, emotional growth and development and their effect on school adjustment and achievement. Field observation of preschool and grade school children required.

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: The Chicano Adolescent
courses.description: The Chicano adolescent's social, intellectual and emotional growth and development. Bicultural pressures from the barrio, family structure, school and achievement values.

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Contemporary Chicana/o Literature
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Chicana and Chicano literature from the 1960s to the present. Considers texts within their cultural, historical, social and political contexts. Relates Chicana/o literature to contemporary U.S. Latina/o writing and to the creative and performing arts.

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Nonprofits and Latinx Communities
courses.description: How nonprofits advance democracy and influence public policy to address urban inequities in Latinx communities. Core concepts and skills development in management, public policy and strategic planning. (CHIC 355 and POSC 355 are the same course)

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Border Cinema
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Examines representations of the U.S.-Mexico border in Mexican and U.S. films from the Mexican Revolution era to the present, as well as border theories in international films and scholarship. (CHIC 369 and CTVA 369 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: The Chicano and Politics
courses.description: Theory of urban politics and evaluation of issues that affect the Chicanos and American society. Evaluations and surveys will be made on political organizations in Hispanic-surnamed communities. (CHIC 460 and POSC 460 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Student to Student Tutorial
courses.description: Learning through teaching. Three hours of work per week expected for each semester unit of credit and may include: tutorial preparations; consulting with instructors; reporting, analyzing and evaluating tutorial experiences. Requires independent research project on topic related to tutoring area.

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Opportunity to study independently under the guidance of the faculty on a subject of special interest and approved by instructor. May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 6 units. Requires approval by the department chair and instructor(s) in charge of directing the study.

courses.subject: CHIC
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: Individual library research or empirical project, with conferences with instructor as necessary, culminating in one or more papers. May be repeated for credit. Requires permission from instructor.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Foundations for Success in CAS and College
courses.description: Introduction to the field of child and adolescent studies for CAS majors as they enter college. Explores developmental concepts and applications to success in college, life, and career. Builds connections with CAS community and campus resources during the transition to college.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Introduction to Child and Adolescent Development
geCategories:
Introduction to Social & Behavioral Sci
Free Course Material
courses.description: Overview and practical application of major developmental concepts from birth to adolescence within different biological, familial, social and cultural contexts.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Explore Core: Migrant Lives
geCategories:
Introduction to Social & Behavioral Sci
Free Course Material
courses.description: Differing sociocultural experiences of different migrant groups. How immigration as a process impacts physical, cognitive and socioemotional development of migrants' children. Educational experiences of migrants and implications for schools and society. (CAS 131, AMST 131 and READ 131 are the same course)

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Thriving as a Transfer Student in CAS and College
courses.description: Introduction to the field of child and adolescent studies for upper-division students transferring from community college and other majors. Developmental concepts and applications to success in college, life and career. Builds connections with CAS community and campus resources.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Child, Family, and Community
courses.description: Relationships between child, family and community members; interaction among systems; influences of gender, abilities, language, culture, race, ethnicity, socio-economic status and political factors; impact of bias and sterotyping; community resources and culturally competent practices to support families.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Responsive Care and Practices for Infants and Toddlers
courses.description: Overview of development among infants and toddlers. Introduces the practice of caring for and teaching of infants and toddlers in group settings. Infant and toddler child care services, emphasizing developmentally appropriate practices.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Introduction to Early Childhood Curriculum
courses.description: Appropriate curriculum and environments for infants and young children, including supporting development through guidance, play, observation and assessment. Development of language and literacy, social skills and emotions, art and creativity, math and science.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Elements of Effective Professional Communication
courses.description: Communication norms and standards in child and adolescent studies. Fosters written and oral communication skills to support students' professional development and their ethical and effective work with diverse children, adolescents and families. Meets upper-division writing requirement for CAS majors.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Inquiry and Methodology in Development
courses.description: Frameworks and methods for conducting and consuming empirical research on the development of children from diverse backgrounds. Introduces scientific method, including developing research questions/hypotheses, surveying, sampling and interpreting statistics. Read, analyze and synthesize research studies retrieved from library databases.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Human Growth and Development
geCategories:
Expl. in Social & Behavioral Sci
Free Course Material
courses.description: Biological/physical, socio-emotional and cognitive development across the lifespan.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Child Development
courses.description: Major concepts, principles, theories and research related to cognitive, linguistic, social, emotional and physical development from birth through adolescence; emphasizes developmentally appropriate practices.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Advanced Study of Infant and Toddler Development
courses.description: Normative and atypical physical, social, emotional and cognitive development for children from birth to three years of age. Child development theories, research strategies and environmental, biological, and cultural influences on the development of young children.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Conception Through Age 8
courses.description: Biological, psychological, cultural and environmental influences on children's physical, cognitive and socioemotional development from conception through age 8. Enhance understanding of developmental research and theories that support cultural competence. Apply knowledge to promote optimal development of children.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Age 9 Through Adolescence
courses.description: Biological, psychological, cultural and environmental influences on physical, cognitive and socioemotional development from age 9 through adolescence. Enhanced understanding of developmental research and theories that support cultural competence. Apply knowledge to promote optimal development of older children and adolescents.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Adolescence and Early Adulthood
courses.description: Human development during and following adolescence. Community resources and services for adolescents and their families. Consequences of adolescent experiences for later development.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Parenting Today
geCategories:
Expl. in Social & Behavioral Sci
Free Course Material
courses.description: Goals and patterns of parenting in context of contemporary, multicultural society; identifies changing demands of parenting infants, children and adolescents; summarizes current scholarly research on relation of parenting practices to child development outcomes.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Child and Adolescent Development in Diverse Family Contexts
courses.description: Patterns and processes of child/adolescent development within families of various cultural/ethnic/social contexts. Identifies multiple theoretical and disciplinary perspectives in studying child and family developmental processes, as well as summarizing the current related scholarly literature.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Advanced Study in Preschool Development
courses.description: Builds on previous foundation classes to explore current issues in child development from age 2 to 6 years. Explores implications for development across the physical, socio-emotional and cognitive domains in the context of diverse families and society.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Curriculum and Early Learning Environments (PK-Grade 3)
courses.description: Developmentally appropriate curriculum and environments for children from age three to age 8 (preschool through 3rd grade). Includes strategies to individualize for children while providing effective developmental support for language and literacy, socio-emotional skills, art and creativity, math, and science.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Learning and Motivation in Early Childhood
courses.description: Building on the foundation developmental classes, this class examines theory and research on children's learning, cognition and motivation with an emphasis on practical applications in early childhood settings. Developmental norms, individual and cultural variations, and curricular strategies.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Adolescents and the Media
courses.description: Summarizes current social, cultural and behavioral research on adolescents and mass media. How teens use, learn, are depicted in, and shape cultural meaning from exposure to television and other electronic media.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Adolescent Sexuality and Intimate Relationships
courses.description: Current trends, potential risks, and opportunities associated with adolescents' involvement in sexual and intimate relationships from a normative developmental perspective. Socio-ecological contexts (e.g., families, peers, culture) of adolescents' sexual and relational attitudes/behaviors are a central focus.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Introductory Practicum in Child and Adolescent Studies
courses.description: Minimum 60 hours of supervised practicum experience in agencies, institutions and organizations serving children, adolescents and/or their families. Analyze experience in relation to developmental theory, professional development skills, cultural competence and developmentally appropriate practice.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Peer Mentoring Academy for Student Success
courses.description: Scholarly, self-reflective work to develop and use advanced communication skills as a Child and Adolescent Studies major peer student mentor under faculty supervision. Requires 35 out-of-class hours on peer mentoring and professional activities.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Practicum Seminar in Early Care and Education
courses.description: Minimum 60 hours of supervised practicum experience in licensed early childhood education settings, working directly with very young children (infants through age 5). Advanced analysis in relation to developmental theory, cultural competence and developmentally appropriate practice.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Practicum in Development in School Settings
courses.description: Minimum 60 hours of supervised practicum experience in elementary school settings serving K-6th grade students, working directly in a classroom. Advanced analysis in relation to California Academic Content Standards, developmental theory, cultural competence and developmentally appropriate practice.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Senior Seminar in Child and Adolescent Development
courses.description: Integrating and applying knowledge, competencies and skills acquired in prerequisite courses to a specific developmental topic (varies by section), including considerations related to biological, psychological, social and cultural factors.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Practicum in Youth and Families in Community Settings
courses.description: Minimum 60 hours of supervised practicum experience in licensed agencies, institutions or organizations that support children, adolescents (up to early 20s) or their families. Analyze experience in relation to developmental theory, professional development skills, cultural competence and developmentally appropriate practice.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Student-to-Student Tutorial
courses.description: Work on student-to-student tutorial and related tasks under the direction of a Child and Adolescent Studies faculty member. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Only 3 units may be taken in a single semester. Requires consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CAS
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individual research project, either library or field, under the direction of a Child and Adolescent Studies faculty member. May be repeated for a maximum of 9 units. Only 6 units may be taken in a single semester.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Fundamental Chinese-A
courses.description: For non-native Chinese speakers. Develop listening and reading comprehension and speaking. Introduces writing and develops cultural awareness to communicate on a basic level. Conducted primarily in Chinese.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: The Art of War and Intercultural Management Strategies
geCategories:
Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
Free Course Material
courses.description: Develop an understanding of Chinese ancient strategies for understanding and managing people in dynamic cultural environments, from an organizational and intercultural management perspective. Requires intermediate to low competency in reading, writing, and speaking Mandarin Chinese (testing may be required). Conducted primarily in Chinese.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Introduction to Chinese Civilization
geCategories:
Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
Free Course Material
courses.description: Social, intellectual and artistic heritage of Chinese civilization. Reading and discussion of characteristics of Chinese civilization while strengthening linguistic facility in Mandarin Chinese. Conducted in Chinese.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Chinese Culture through Cinema and Literature
geCategories:
Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
Free Course Material
courses.description: The development of modern Chinese culture and society. Multicultural analysis of global issues through various media, including subtitled films and literature. Conducted primarily in English.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Introduction to Cinema and Television
courses.description: The history, structure and function of the radio, TV and film industry. Current issues, relevance to society, employment options and other topics.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Inside The Movies
courses.description: Artistic, technical, and economic aspects of making and distributing feature films. Each week, different guests from Hollywood discuss their work in the film industry.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: TV Studio Production
courses.description: Introduction to multi-camera, live-to-drive television studio production. Theory and practice of producing multi-camera, studio television programs. Students crew all positions, including producer, director, associate director, technical director, floor manager, camera operator, audio engineer, etc.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Production for Non-Production Track
courses.description: Introduction to single-camera video production designed for non-production students. Theory and practice of producing projects on location. Preproduction, production and post-production using digital cameras and nonlinear editing.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Writing Short Scripts
courses.description: Techniques for writing short-form scripts for film and video. Analysis of short films in relation to scriptwriting concepts. Develop and critique student-written short scripts.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Language of Film
courses.description: Visual and syntactic components of the motion picture. Detailed analysis of frame, line, space, shape, image size, movement, tone, color and structuring of visual images.

sections.instructor: Robert W. Davis, Robert W. Davis, Robert W. Davis, Robert W. Davis
Robert W. Davis, Robert W. Davis, Robert W. Davis, Robert W. Davis

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Critical Studies: Cinema
courses.description: Formal film analysis in terms of filmic and stylistic elements. Explores how films produce meanings.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Critical Studies: Television
courses.description: Formal structures (formats, narratives, genres) and styles of American television. Analyzes how the medium makes its meaning.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Film and Television Narrative: The Writer's Perspective
courses.description: Narrative structures as applied to screenwriting for motion pictures and television. Study the various elements that form a narrative screenplay and identify and analyze them in finished films and TV series.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Diversity in Television
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Critical examination and analysis of the representation of minority groups in American and global television. The intersectional representation of age, disability, gender, race/ethnicity, religion, sexual identity, nation and socioeconomic class.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Audio Production
courses.description: Advanced audio projects for radio, TV, film and the internet, including digital storage and distribution. Complete the audio production process, from pre- through postproduction, applying aesthetic concepts and hands-on skills. (2 hours discussion, 3 hours laboratory)

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Production 1
courses.description: Essentials of shot design, coverage, editing and sound for production students. Planning, directing, shooting, picture editing, and sound capturing and editing for various narrative projects.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: The Video Game Industry
courses.description: This course utilizes readings and guest speakers to provide an overview of the video game industry. Students will explore stages of game development, gaining insight into research, design, production, marketing, etc. It will also examine industry trends and career opportunities.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Story Structure
courses.description: Analyze and develop script structure and viable, narrative story elements. Acts, scenes, premises, conflict, plots, characters, action, etc. Write critical analyses of professional scripts and author own treatments. Meets upper-division writing requirement for CTVA majors. One or more sections may be offered in any online format.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: TV Scriptwriting: Drama
courses.description: Theory, principles and practice of writing for episodic television dramas. Students analyze scripts, study program episodes and develop and write an original story and spec script for a current one hour, prime-time TV drama.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: American TV: Beginnings-1980
courses.description: History of American television programming up to 1980. TV series in the context of changing trends and influences in the industry.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Media Literacy
courses.description: Media literacy: what it is and its importance to lifelong learning. Evaluate and decode the various messages the media deliver, with a primary focus on radio, television, films and new media.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Contemporary World Cinema
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: National cinemas, film movements, filmmakers and the increasing internationalization of the world film industry from 1990 to the present, in terms of stylistic elements and how they are shaped by the circumstances in which they are produced and received.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Film Genres
courses.description: Analyze film genres in terms of their formal and stylistic elements and how they are shaped by the historical, cultural, political, social and industry-related circumstances in which they are produced and received. May be repeated for credit with different topics for a maximum of 9 units.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Producing for Film and Video
courses.description: The task of the producer in film and television from concept to delivery. Fundamentals of breaking down and preparing a script for production, managing a budget and the logistics of producing a short film.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Editing Film and Video
courses.description: Intensive production workshop on editing film and video. Editorial logistics and aesthetics.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Directing Film and TV
courses.description: Analyzing the role of the director in features and television. Directing for narrative features and television, including blocking with the camera and working with actors. Emphasizes collaboration with the cinematographer and crew.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Management in CTVA
courses.description: Management structure and issues in the CTVA industry. Audience measurement, distribution, finance, personnel, programming, regulation and sales. May include applied experience with college media activities.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Film and TV Marketing
courses.description: Film and TV content marketing is evolving rapidly, driven by technological, market and consumer trends. Provides a foundational understanding of the current methodologies for marketing and promoting film and TV content across all platforms. (CTVA 482 and MKTG 482 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Mass Media Internship
courses.description: Supervised fieldwork at a radio, TV or film organization. Skill development and understanding of industry operation through hands-on experience and networking. Must submit an application through the CTVA Internship Office one semester prior to enrolling. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Practical, Ethical and Business Considerations of Generative AI in Screenwriting
courses.description: Use of Generative AI by screenwriters. Experiment with AI during the ideation, outlining and scene writing phases of screenplay development. Research ethical and business issues surrounding AI.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Story Structure and Draft
courses.description: Structure of storytelling in film, linear and non-linear, American Asian and European templates. Product-oriented towards detailed film treatment to serve as outline of screenplay and initial pages of screenplay.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Sitcom: Spec and Draft
courses.description: Write two half-hour situation comedy scripts in correct format, as well as create a premise for an original half-hour comedy series.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Genres for Writers
courses.description: Examining film genres classic to revisionist and the constant evolution and hybridization of genres and how a screenwriter can implement and benefit from understanding of genre components.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Screenplay: Rewrite
courses.description: For students who have completed a first draft of a full-length screenplay. Complete a rewrite/polish of their scripts, learning skills to prepare it for production and entrance into the marketplace.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Writing Project #1
courses.description: From concept to outline to realized film script, an accelerated class focused on working under deadline and reacting to and implementing specific notes from instructor.

courses.subject: CTVA
courses.title: Building The Screenwriter's Portfolio
courses.description: A successful writing career with longevity and positive impact relies on creativity, resilience, purpose and strategic planning. How to manage ideas as intellectual property and the best ways to develop, pitch and market them.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Computer-Aided Architectural and Civil Engineering Drafting
courses.description: Architectural and civil engineering drawing with the aid of computer-aided drafting techniques; grading plans, engineering drawings (including standard structural, electrical and hydraulic details) of buildings, bridges, dams and civil engineering structures. Bill of Materials. (3 hours laboratory)

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Statics
courses.description: Vectorial treatment of statics of particles and rigid bodies. Free body diagrams. Applications to problems of equilibrium (two and three dimensions) of structural and mechanical force systems. Trusses, frames and machines. Friction problems. Centroids and moments of inertia.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Dynamics
courses.description: Kinematics and kinetics of particles and rigid bodies, kinetics of rigid bodies in three dimension, Newton's laws, work and energy, impulse and momentum. Solution of problems using vector approach.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Mechanics of Materials
courses.description: Stress and deformation analysis for axial load, torsion, flexure, and combined forces. Analysis of simple statically indeterminate structures. Deflection and stress analysis of beams. Stability of columns. Strain energy and ultimate resistance. Interactive relationships between analysis and design.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Earthquake Impact on Structures
courses.description: Geological aspects of earthquakes as they apply to building safety; introduction to earthquake-related problems and building damages caused by historic earthquakes. Destruction aspects of earthquakes, preparedness for large earthquakes and how to protect structural and non-structural parts of buildings.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Structural Analysis
courses.description: Forces and displacements in statically determinate and indeterminate elastic structures by force and displacement methods. Approximate methods of analysis. Matrix formulation of structural analysis and computer applications. Introduction to structural design.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Reinforced Concrete Design
courses.description: Design for bending, shear, axial force and combined loading. Ultimate strength and serviceability requirements for beams, columns and slabs. Safety, reliability and cost considerations. Design project conforming to the latest ACI code. Apply professional computer program.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Structural Steel Design
courses.description: Design for bending, torsion, shear, axial forces, combined loadings. Design of built-up girders, composite construction. Design of shear and moment connections. Design project using professional practice standards. LRFD method. Safety, reliability and cost considerations. Professional computer program. (3 hours lecture)

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Engineering Hydraulics Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to experimental hydraulics in open channel and pipe flows, including measurements of discharge, depth, velocity, force and friction coefficients. Hydraulic model laws and report writing. (3 hours laboratory)

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Soil Mechanics
courses.description: Soil properties and soil action as related to problems encountered in engineering structures; consolidation, shear strength, stability and lateral earth pressures.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Soil Mechanics Laboratory
courses.description: Behavior and properties of soils. Application to foundation design, liquefaction and seepage.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Foundation Design
courses.description: Footings and retaining walls. Mat and piled foundations for structures. Design project to standards of professional practice using latest codes and standards. Consideration for safety, reliability and cost. (3 hours lecture)

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Construction Engineering
courses.description: Engineering construction planning equipment and methods. Construction management. Critical path method. Construction of buildings, bridges, highways, foundations and dams. Consideration for safety and reliability.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Environmental Engineering
courses.description: Planning and controlling the environment; wastewater treatment and disposal; solid waste management; air pollution; radiation protection; housing and residential environment.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Engineering Economics and Professionalism
courses.description: Development, evaluation and presentation of design alternatives for engineering systems and projects using principles of engineering economy and cost benefit analysis. Engineering profession, professional ethics and related topics. (Not available for use on graduate study plans.) (EGEC 401, EGCE 401, and EGME 401 are the same course.)

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Structural Dynamics
courses.description: Free and forced vibrations of discrete and continuous systems. Matrix formulation and normal coordinates analysis. Response of structures to impulse and earthquake loads. Application to structural design problems and comparison with code prescribed forces.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Design of Hydraulic Structures
courses.description: Applications of hydraulic principles to design of various structures, including spillways, energy dissipaters, outlet works, storm drains, culverts and water distribution systems. Use of computers in design process.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Water Quality Engineering
courses.description: Engineering approaches for maintaining water quality; water quality parameters and standards; physical, chemical and biological processes of water and wastewater treatment systems; theoretical and design aspects of kinetics and reactor theory.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Senior Design
courses.description: Real-world culminating design experience in a multidisciplinary civil engineering project. Use of professional practice codes and standards; realistic cost and safety constraints.
