Huda Munjy, Kristijan Kolozvari, Melad Hanna
Huda Munjy, Kristijan Kolozvari, Melad Hanna

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Senior Projects
courses.description: Independent design projects. Formal report to be submitted after completion of project work. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Requires adviser and department chair consent.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Construction Methods and Equipment for Heavy Construction Engineering
courses.description: Methods and equipment for construction foundations, highways, airfields, bridges, ports, harbors, dams, nuclear power plants and industrial facilities. Quality control and construction failures.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Cost Estimating and Bidding Strategy
courses.description: Management and cost control of large capital projects. Capital cost estimation, value prediction and control, cost and schedule control and management of mega projects.

courses.subject: EGCE
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units (three units per semester). Requires classified graduate status and formal approval of Civil Engineering Graduate Committee, graduate adviser and department head.

courses.subject: CNSM
courses.title: Think Like Einstein
courses.description: Science influences everyday lives. To think like a scientist (and an informed citizen), students need skills in critical thinking, argumentation and logical reasoning. Course develops these skills and provides practice applying them to a range of topics. This course is intended for first time freshmen.

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Introduction to Phonetics
courses.description: Analysis and description of speech at the segmental and suprasegmental levels. Practice using the International Phonetic Alphabet for broad and narrow transcription. Overview of speech production.

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Introduction to Research in Communication Sciences and Disorders
courses.description: Understanding and using professional literature in communication sciences and disorders and using that literature to generate a formal research paper. A passing grade fulfills the course requirement of the university upper-division baccalaureate writing requirement for communicative disorders majors.

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Introduction to Sign Language
courses.description: Overview of the deaf experience and the options for communication in the deaf community. Use of American Sign Language and finger spelling at the introductory level.

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Child Language and Phonological Disorders
courses.description: Language and phonological disorders in children. Speech/language profiles of special populations and contemporary approaches to assessment and intervention. Practice analyzing child speech/language samples.

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Audiology and Audiometry
courses.description: Characteristics of hearing disorders, including etiologies and risk factors. Methods and procedures used in assessing the auditory system including current topics of interest. Partially fulfills the requirements for state audiometrist certificate.

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Clinical Methods and Procedures
courses.description: General principles and procedures for assessment and treatment of individuals with communicative disorders. Lecture, demonstration, clinical observations and supervised clinical experience.

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Internship in Communication Sciences and Disorders
courses.description: Minimum of 120 hours of supervised fieldwork at a CICE-approved internship site. Practical application of academic knowledge within the field of Communication Sciences and Disorders via experience in a clinical or professional setting.

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Open to upper-division students in communication sciences and disorders only with signed consent form from department chair. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Specialty Clinic
courses.description: Supervised/specialized clinical experiences that address the needs of: adults seeking gender-affirming voice and communication modifications, using evidence-based practices; or children and adults who require aided augmentative alternative communication (AAC) systems to support ldaily communication.

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Autism Spectrum Disorders in Speech-Language Pathology
courses.description: Communication disorders in children with autism spectrum disorders (current theories, diagnostic process, co-occurring conditions, the role of speech-language pathologists in multi-disciplinary approaches to assessment and intervention planning, critical review of relevant research).

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Seminar in Voice Disorders
courses.description: Review classification of voice disorders (perceptually); examine instrumental assessment of such disorders (acoustically); and emphasize a comprehensive physiological, perceptual and acoustic work-up of individual cases. Requires approved Individual Student Schedule.

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Seminar: Speech and Hearing Service in Schools
courses.description: Problems and challenges unique to the student clinician in organizing and managing the speech and hearing program in the school. Clinician's role; planning, scheduling, case finding, treatment program reporting and other responsibilities.

courses.subject: COMD
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: Open to graduate students only with signed consent from department chair. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Writing for Mass Media
courses.description: Principles and practices of writing for major types of mass communications media. Content, organization, conciseness and clarity. All Fullerton campus lectures online, laboratory in classroom. Requires typing ability. (2 hours lecture, 2 hours laboratory)

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Digital Reporting and Production
courses.description: Develop expertise in news reporting and production for digital platforms, emphasizing visual storytelling and production. News content contribution to student media.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Mass Communication in Modern Society
courses.description: Internet, newspapers, magazines, film, radio and television; their significance as social instruments and economic entities in modern society.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Mass Media and Diversity
courses.description: Analyzes the representations of marginalized groups in mass media and popular culture. Evaluates gender, race, sexuality, religion, and other identities. Designed to make students more critical producers and consumers of the media.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Digital Foundations
courses.description: Develop ability to create and evaluate multimedia content. Preparation for digital portfolio graduation requirement.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Visual Reporting
courses.description: Image creation for publication in print and/or screen media. Convergence of the basic principles and practices of digital photography, digital imaging, graphic design and web page production for journalism-based visual problem solving.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Studio Photography
courses.description: Creative and effective use of images in print and/or screen publications within advertising, public relations, entertainment studies and other commercial, persuasive communication contexts.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Global Media
courses.description: Major mass communication systems, both democratic and totalitarian, and the means by which news and propaganda are conveyed internationally. The role of media in the process of globalization.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Mass Media Effects
courses.description: The role mass media communications play in all human activity with heavy emphasis on the effects of mass media on the political, social and economic fabric of America.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Feature Article Writing
courses.description: Nonfiction writing for newspapers and magazines; sources, methods and markets.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Public Affairs Reporting
courses.description: Reporting public interest news such as courts, education, finance, government, police and urban problems. COMM 407 recommended.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Principles of Entertainment and Tourism Communications
courses.description: Structure and commercial functions of the entertainment and tourism industries. The central role of communication in industry technologies and professional practices. Career opportunities associated with these fields.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Principles of Advertising
courses.description: Overview of the advertising industry and its specializations. Contemporary functions, strategies, media, ethics and technology, as well as the role of integrated marketing communication.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Writing for the Advertising Industry
courses.description: Develop persuasive communication skills essential for success within the advertising industry. Write strategic advertising copy for various target audiences across multiple platforms. Must earn a "C" (2.0) or better to continue taking advertising courses.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Advertising Media
courses.description: Plan, execute and control advertising media programs. Basic data and characteristics of the media. Buying and selling process, techniques and methods in media planning process. Audience measurement and media analysis.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Advertising Creative Strategy and Execution I
courses.description: Writing copy and layout advertisements, based on study of sales appeals, attention factors and illustrations. (2 hours lecture, 2 hours activity)

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Principles and Ethics of Public Relations
courses.description: Social, behavioral, psychological, ethical, economic and political foundations of public relations, and the theories of public relations as a communications discipline.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Radio-Audio Operations
courses.description: Concepts and practices of radio station and audio broadcast operations, including programming, sales, promotion, traffic, billing, production, news, research and engineering. Work in traditional and online formats.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: TV News Production
courses.description: Writing, production and evaluation of television news. Discussion of TV reporting techniques and problems. Cover events and produce TV news in lab. (2 hours lecture, 2 hours lab)

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Principles of Communication Research
courses.description: Research methods used to assess the effects of print, broadcast and film communications on audience attitudes, opinions, knowledge and behavior. Research design and data analysis in communications research.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Communications Technologies
courses.description: Issues surrounding communications technologies. Recent developments in technology, impact of government, industry and economic factors, historical overview and implications for social change. Technological developments. Applications to all areas of mass communications.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Public Relations Capstone - Bateman Case Study Competition
courses.description: Provides opportunities to apply classroom education and internship experiences to plan and implement a strategic public relations campaign for a real-world client by competing in the PRSA Bateman Case Study Competition.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Magazine Editing and Production
courses.description: Produce a high-quality magazine and learn about the dynamics of magazine production and the magazine industry. May repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Sports Reporting
courses.description: Advanced reporting and writing skills in sports reporting. Combine an awareness of techniques and resources with an abundance of writing models and field experiences.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Entertainment and Society
courses.description: Role of entertainment and tourism in modern society. Uses theoretical and historical approaches to explore how factors such as culture, technology, economics and politics intersect with the entertainment we create and consume.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Entertainment Industry Studies
courses.description: Variable topics course that focuses on specific entertainment industries, issues, organizations, trends and/or functions. May be repeated once for credit with different topic.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Capstone - Entertainment and Tourism Communications
courses.description: Prepares for entertainment industry careers by combining theory with applied principles and analytical skills in examining and developing case studies. Students plan and execute their own campaigns and projects. A "C-" (1.7) or better is required to pass course.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Advertising and Brand Communication Management
courses.description: Theory and techniques for planning, directing and evaluating advertising and brand communication programs, with emphasis on media-message strategies. Managerial approach with case studies to the solution of brand communications problems.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Capstone - Advertising Campaigns
courses.description: Advertising campaigns, including applied research, writing and utilization of print and electronic mass media. Design of complete campaigns from idea to prediction readiness. A "C-" (1.7) or better is required to pass this course.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Advertising Media Sales
courses.description: Advertising media sales, emphasizing print, special event, online and social media platforms. Work directly with the Daily Titan advertising staff while developing personal sales techniques, media sales strategies and supporting marketing tactics.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Internet Advertising and Promotional Communications
courses.description: Internet advertising and marketing issues and ideas. Evaluate, develop and execute Internet-based advertising and promotional campaigns.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Broadcast Advertising
courses.description: Theoretical and practical exposure to the field of broadcast advertising from an agency perspective, including positioning, creative brief writing, strategy, script development and analysis, storyboarding and pitching.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Capstone - Public Relations Management
courses.description: Analyze systems and strategies for planning public relations campaigns and solving/preventing problems. Individual, team case studies, in corporate development of proposals; actual use of tools in addition to role playing presentations to management. "C-" (1.7) or better required to pass.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Current Topics in Public Relations
courses.description: Examines advanced public relations concepts and skills in specialized areas. Health public relations campaigns; public relations in U.S. higher education. May be repeated once for extra elective units only.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Corporate and Nonprofit Public Relations
courses.description: Public relations strategies and tactics used in today's increasingly sophisticated and maturing corporate and nonprofit marketplaces. Professional guest speakers and in-class simulations/exercises. Fund raising, corporate and social responsibility, media relations, and technology and ethical issues.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Capstone - Daily Titan News
courses.description: Students form the editorial staff of Daily Titan, the university newspaper; training in print and online journalism. Meets four hours per week for critiques in news reporting, writing, editing and production. (more than 9 hours laboratory.) Must pass with a "C-" (1.7) or better.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Capstone - TV News
courses.description: Produce, report and anchor live television newscast OC News. Learn online journalism. (2 hours lecture, 3 hours lab.) May be taken for credit for a maximum of six units. Must pass with a "C-" (1.7) or better.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Capstone - ADV/PR/ETC Student Agency
courses.description: Work in a student-run agency to plan and conduct integrated communications campaigns involving advertising, public relations, and tourism/ entertainment/ event planning. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Mass Media Internship
courses.description: 120 hours minimum of supervised fieldwork at a CICE-approved internship site. Practical application of academic knowledge within the student's field of concentration via hands-on experience in the professional arena. Attendance at an orientation session is required. Details at: communications.fullerton.edu/internship.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Student-to-Student Tutorial
courses.description: Under faculty supervision, provides tutorial assistance in a communications course. May involve small group demonstrations and discussions, individual tutoring and evaluation of student performance as appropriate. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units either separately or in combination with COMM 499. Requires superior performance in a similar or equivalent course.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Event Planning and Management
courses.description: Plan, produce and promote public events to meet communication objectives. Hands-on applications to COMM Week, Newport Beach Film Festival, Fullerton Arboretum or other events. May be repeated once for extra elective units only.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individually supervised mass media projects and research on campus and in the community. May involve newspaper and magazine publishers, radio and television stations, and public relations agencies. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units, either separately or in combination with COMM 496. Requires consent of department chair.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Theory and Literature of Communications
courses.description: Theories and research on communication processes and effects; source, media, message, audience and content variables; types, sources and uses of communication literature. Graduate seminar.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Social Science Research in Communications
courses.description: Social-scientific research design and analysis and the study of communication processes and effects. Graduate seminar.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Ethical Problems of the Mass Media
courses.description: Criticisms of specific functions of the mass media and public relations. Three sections: history of criticism; problem areas of the media; and practitioner response to criticism.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Advanced Communications Management
courses.description: Up-to-date assessment of general management and communications management techniques, and helps equip the student for management positions in advertising, journalism, public relations and broadcasting.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Advertising in Modern Society
courses.description: Assessing the impact of advertising on society, the culture and economy. Philosophical rather than technical examinations of critical issues and problems such as economic and social effects of advertising, effects of value and life styles, ethics and regulation.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Graduate Mass Media Internship
courses.description: Supervised practical work experience with media outlets, advertising and promotion agencies, public relations firms, film companies, etc. Involves cooperative efforts of departmental faculty and employers. Current and innovative techniques in research, management and creative activities while offering practical experience. Requires consent of graduate adviser.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Project
courses.description: Complete creative project in a sequence beyond regularly offered coursework. Requires consent of graduate coordinator.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: Complete a thesis in a sequence beyond regularly offered coursework. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Requires consent of graduate coordinator.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: Individually supervised mass media projects or research for graduate students. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Requires consent of graduate coordinator.

courses.subject: CPLT
courses.title: Classical Mythology in World Literature
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Greek and Roman myths which have been of continuing significance in Western world literature.

courses.subject: CPLT
courses.title: World Literature to 1650
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Asian and Western literature from the beginning to 1650.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Programming Lecture
courses.description: Introduction computer science and computer programming, including designing programs; sequential execution; variables, assignment and arithmetic; control flow, Boolean logic, selection and loops; input/output; functions; debugging; practical applications; and development methodologies. (50-minute lecture)

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Programming Lab
courses.description: Introduction to computer science and computer programming, including designing programs; sequential execution; variables, assignment and arithmetic; control flow, Boolean logic, selection and loops; input/output; functions; debugging; practical applications; and development methodologies.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Object Oriented Programming Lecture
courses.description: The object-oriented programming paradigm, including classes, objects, member variables and functions; exceptions, inheritance, templates, encapsulation, decoupling and class design best practices. Advanced program design, including iterators, operator overloading, recursion and dynamic memory allocation (50-minute lecture).

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Object-Oriented Programming Lab
courses.description: Apply object-oriented programming concepts, including classes, objects, member variables and functions; exceptions, inheritance, templates, encapsulation, decoupling and class design best practices. Advanced program design, including iterators, operator overloading, recursion and dynamic memory allocation.

sections.instructor: Paul Salvador Inventado, Akshay Bhagwat Nimse

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Data Structures
courses.description: Classical data structures: vector, linked list, stack, queue, binary search tree, and graph representations. Worst-case analysis, amortized analysis, and big-O notation. Object-oriented and recursive implementation of data structures. Self-resizing vectors and self-balancing trees. Empirical performance measurement.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Python Programming
courses.description: Concepts of computing, domain-specific problem solving with computing technologies. Methodologies, tools and the application development process. Variables, expressions, control flow, functions, standard libraries, packages, data structures, files, modularization, integration. Develop functional applications. (2 hours lecture, 2 hours lab per week)

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Computer Organization and Assembly Language
courses.description: Digital logic and architecture of a computer system, machine level representation of data, memory system organization, structure of low-level computer languages. Machine, assembly, and macro language programming. Principles of assembler operation, input-output programming, interrupt/exception handling. Laboratory programming assignments. (2 hours lecture, 2 hours laboratory)

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Cybersecurity Foundations and Principles
courses.description: Security goals, security systems, access controls, networks and security, integrity, cryptography fundamentals, authentication. Attacks: software, network, website; management considerations, security standards in government and industry; security issues in requirements, architecture, design, implementation, testing, operation, maintenance, acquisition and services.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Applied Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Concepts of Artificial Intelligence, application software and open-source projects. Understanding AI capabilities, AI applications, their impact and ethical issues. Identifying domain-specific problems and solving them with AI technologies and related open-source projects.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Professional Ethics in Computing
courses.description: Ethics and moral philosophy as applied to software and digital artifacts. Notions of rights, responsibilities, property, ownership, privacy, security, and professional ethics. Security obligations. Intellectual propertystatutes, licenses, and their terms. Oral and written reports are required.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Compilers and Languages
courses.description: Basic concepts of programming languages and principles of translation. Topics include history of programming languages, various programming paradigms, language design issues and criteria, design of compilers for modern programming languages.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: File Structures and Database Systems
courses.description: Fundamental theories and design of database systems, the Structured Query Language (SQL), basic concepts and techniques of data organization in secondary storage. Topics include introduction to database systems, ER model, relational model, index structures and hashing techniques.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Algorithm Engineering
courses.description: Algorithm design using classical patterns: exhaustive search, divide and conquer, randomization, hashing, reduction, dynamic programming, and the greedy method. Asymptotic and experimental efficiency analysis. NP-completeness and decidability. Implementing algorithms to solve practical problems.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Web Front-End Engineering
courses.description: Concepts and architecture of interactive web applications, including markup, stylesheets and behavior. Functional and object-oriented aspects of JavaScript. Model-view design patterns, templates and frameworks. Client-side technologies for asynchronous events, real-time interaction and access to back-end web services.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Operating Systems Concepts
courses.description: Resource management, memory organization, input/output, control process synchronization and other concepts as related to the objectives of multi-user operating systems.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Cryptography
courses.description: Introduction to cryptography and steganography. Encryption, cryptographic hashing, certificates, and signatures. Classical, symmetric-key, and public-key ciphers. Block modes of operation. Cryptanalysis including exhaustive search, man-in-the-middle, and birthday attacks. Programing projects involving implementation of cryptographic systems.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Foundations of Software Engineering
courses.description: Basic concepts, principles, methods, techniques and practices of software engineering. All aspects of the software engineering fields. Use Computer-Aided Software Engineering (CASE) tools.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Data Science and Big Data
courses.description: Techniques for data preparation, exploratory analysis, statistical modeling, machine learning and visualization. Methods for analyzing different types of data, such as natural language and time-series, from emerging applications, including Internet-of-Things. Big data platforms. Projects with real-world data.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Game Design and Production
courses.description: Current and future technologies and market trends in game design and production. Game technologies, basic building tools for games and the process of game design, development and production.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Mobile Device Application Programming
courses.description: Introduction to developing applications for mobile devices, including but not limited to runtime environments, development tools and debugging tools used in creating applications for mobile devices. Use emulators in lab. Students must provide their own mobile devices.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Mobile Device Application Programming for Android
courses.description: Introduction to developing applications for Android mobile devices, including but not limited to runtime environments, development tools and debugging tools used in creating applications for mobile devices. Use emulators in lab. Students must provide own mobile devices.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Computer System Architecture
courses.description: Computer performance, price/performance, instruction set design and examples. Processor design, pipelining, memory hierarchy design and input/output subsystems.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Web Back-End Engineering
courses.description: Design and architecture of large-scale web applications. Techniques for scalability, session management and load balancing. Dependency injection, application tiers, message queues, web services and REST architecture. Caching and eventual consistency. Data models, partitioning and replication in relational and non-relational databases.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Cloud Computing and Security
courses.description: Cloud computing and cloud security, distributed computing, computer clusters, grid computing, virtual machines and virtualization, cloud computing platforms and deployment models, cloud programming and software environments, vulnerabilities and risks of cloud computing, cloud infrastructure protection, data privacy and protection.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Web Security
courses.description: Web application security concepts, including authentication, access control, sensitive data protection,  SQL attacks, cross-site scripting, and request forgery. Implement hands-on security mechanisms and testing.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Network Security
courses.description: Vulnerabilities of network protocols, attacks targeting confidentiality, integrity and availability of data transmitted across networks, and methods for diagnosing and closing security gaps through hands-on exercises. Aligns with the National Centers of Academic Excellence curriculum.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Malware Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to principles and practices of malware analysis. Topics include static and dynamic code analysis, data decoding, analysis tools, debugging, shellcode analysis, reverse engineering of stealthy malware and written presentation of analysis results.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Blockchain Technologies
courses.description: Digital assets as a medium of exchange to secure financial transactions; decentralized and distributed ledgers that record verifiable transactions; smart contracts and Ethereum; Bitcoin mechanics and mining; the cryptocurrency ecosystem; blockchain mechanics and applications.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Software Design
courses.description: Concepts of software modeling, software process and some tools. Object-oriented analysis and design and Unified process. Some computer-aided software engineering (CASE) tools will be recommended to use for doing homework assignments.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Software Testing
courses.description: Software testing techniques, reporting problems effectively and planning testing projects. Students apply what they learned throughout the course to a sample application that is either commercially available or under development.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Software Architecture
courses.description: Basic principles and practices of software design and architecture. High-level design, software architecture, documenting software architecture, software and architecture evaluation, software product lines and some considerations beyond software architecture.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Software Process
courses.description: Practical guidance for improving the software development process. How to establish, maintain and improve software processes. Exposure to agile processes, ISO 12207 and CMMI.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Computer Communications
courses.description: Introduction to digital data communications. Terminology, networks and their components, common-carrier services, telecommunication facilities, terminals, error control, multiplexing and concentration techniques.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Edge AI: Principles and Practices
courses.description: Edge AI principles and applications in real-world scenarios. Various open-source software frameworks and AI models used for developing Edge AI applications. Key programming languages, design patterns and open-source tools for edge AI apps.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Using computers to simulate human intelligence. Production systems, pattern recognition, problem solving, searching game trees, knowledge representation and logical reasoning. Programming in AI environments.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
courses.description: Design, implement and analyze machine learning algorithms, including supervised learning and unsupervised learning algorithms. Methods to address uncertainty. Projects with real-world data.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Principles of Computer Graphics
courses.description: Examine and analyze computer graphics, software structures, display processor organization, graphical input/output devices, display files. Algorithmic techniques for clipping, windowing, character generation and viewpoint transformation.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Computational Bioinformatics
courses.description: Algorithmic approaches to biological problems. Specific topics include motif finding, genome rearrangement, DNA sequence comparison, sequence alignment, DNA sequencing, repeat finding and gene expression analysis.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Concepts of natural language, natural language processing, understanding and generation. Designing and building various language models using computational approaches to solve common natural language problems, as well as other real-world problems.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar in Computer Science
courses.description: Review of foundational computer science theories and principles, real-world application development methods and processes, and industry practices. Survey of modern computing technologies. Research methods. Identification of research or practical application problems. Writing and presenting a proposal for a capstone project.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Senior Capstone Project in Computer Science
courses.description: A computer science research or real-world level of application development project. Business communication. Presenting the results to a wide range of audiences. Demonstrating the culminating experience of the practicum in computer science. Writing a final project report and technical documents such as user manuals, installation guides, feasibility study reports.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Special topic in computer science, selected in consultation with and completed under the supervision of instructor. May be repeated for a maximum of 9 units of Undergraduate credit. Requires approval by the Computer Science chair.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Advanced Algorithms
courses.description: Design and analysis of sophisticated algorithms and data structures. Lower, tight and pseudo-polynomial bounds. Randomization, approximation and special-purpose data structures. Algorithmic frameworks, such as maximum flow and linear programming. CPSC 335 recommended.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Systems and Software Standards and Requirements
courses.description: SESC framework and the IEEE Software Engineering Standards. Establishing the following standards: Software Life Cycle Processes, Work Product Standards, Process Standards, Requirement Analysis and Management and System Integration. Introduces CMMI framework; discuss number of practical lessons. CPSC 362 recommended.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Software Verification and Validation
courses.description: Theory and practice of software verification and validation (V&V), including software integrity levels, minimum V&V tasks, walkthroughs, inspections and clean room. Topics include: white-box and black-box testing, boundary value analysis, equivalence class partitioning, unit testing, functional testing and test plans. CPSC 362 recommended.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Advanced Software Process
courses.description: Advanced guidance for defining and improving the software development process. Concepts of software maturity framework, principles of process improvement and software process assessment. Current topics such as CMMI and SCAMPI. CPSC 362 recommended.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Modern Software Management
courses.description: Modern project management methodologies and techniques. Software development process. Planning, estimating, organizing, directing, monitoring, controlling software projects and managing risks. Other related software management issues, such as infrastructure, quality software development, project and product metrics and external factors. CPSC 362 recommended.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Software Measurement
courses.description: Current software measurement practices. Topics include:  establishing an effective software metrics program; measuring software product, project and process; applying Statistical Process Control and other statistical techniques. High maturity concepts defined in CMMI model will be discussed. Stresses a practitioner-based approach. CPSC 362 recommended.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Advanced Computer Networking
courses.description: System-oriented view of computer network design, protocol implementation, networking, high-speed networking, network management, computer network performance issues. CPSC 471 recommended.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Advanced Blockchain Technologies
courses.description: A holistic experience for different types of blockchain development. The ins and outs of blockchain and Ethereum from a developer perspective, along with smart contract security and best practices.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Knowledge Representation and Reasoning
courses.description: A field of artificial intelligence representing information about the world in a form that a computer system can use to solve complex tasks. Representing knowledge symbolically for automated reasoning; inference algorithms; logic programming; Semantic Web; reasoning under uncertainty; Requires project. CPSC 481 recommended.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Seminar in Computer Science
courses.description: Research methods in computer science. Current technology trends and research topics. Verification of computer science theories and principles. Identification of practical application development and/or research problems. Presentations on selected topics and problems. Writing a proposal for a capstone graduate project.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Project
courses.description: Conduct a computer science research or development project proposed in the selected topic, complete it, write a final project report, and present the results in partial fulfillment of the requirements for the master's degree. Classified graduate standing and approval of the computer science graduate adviser are required to enroll.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: Requires approval of the Computer Science graduate adviser.

courses.subject: CPSC
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: Special topic in computer science, selected in consultation with and completed under supervision of a full-time faculty member. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. CPSC 589 recommended. Requires approval of Computer Science department chair.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Career and Life Planning
courses.description: Career, personal and educational awareness. Strategies include integrating skills, abilities, interests and values into the career search. Decision-making and goal setting.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Leadership Skills and Personal Development
courses.description: Leadership concepts and skills, including psychological process, conflict resolution, counseling and human service skills. Becoming aware of personal leadership styles; maintaining vitality through physical and mental health. (HUSR 350 and COUN 350 are the same course).

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: The Counseling Profession
courses.description: Counseling as a mental health profession, including its history, current functions and future directions. The counselor as a professional, including educational goals, personal values and cultural understandings. Opportunity to observe master counselors at work.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Career and Lifestyle Development
courses.description: Survey of career and lifestyle development throughout the lifespan. Major theories and strategies in career counseling. Integrating knowledge of career development with the practice of counseling. (COUN 502 and PSYC 502 are the same course).

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Pre-Practicum
courses.description: Basic counseling skills, including establishing a therapeutic relationship, facilitating client self-exploration and understanding how one's values influence the counseling process. Crisis intervention. Extensive role play practice.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Human Development and Functioning
courses.description: Human development from infancy to old age, and its effect on individuals, couples and family relationships. Implications for counseling; role of cultural/social contexts and social stressors; role of human sexuality in development.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Research in Counseling
courses.description: Applied research methods, critical evaluation of research in counseling and completion of literature review for anticipated COUN 597 project.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Diagnosis and Treatment Planning
courses.description: Advanced study of the latest edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Health Disorders (DSM). A comprehensive bio/psychosocial/cultural view, focusing on diagnosis and assessment of major diagnostic categories, as well as integrative treatment planning

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Psychopharmacology for Counselors
courses.description: Introduces biochemical basis of behavior and a general knowledge of the effects and side effects of the major classes of psychotropic drugs. Such knowledge is to make appropriate referrals and a comprehensive approach to treatment.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Professional, Ethical and Legal Issues in Counseling
courses.description: Current ethical and legal standards in practice of counseling and marriage and family therapy. Issues related to child/partner/elder abuse and substance abuse. Role of counselor values, work contexts and client-centered perspective in ethical decision-making. Licensing laws and process. Must pass with a B or better to advance to COUN 530.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Systems of Family Counseling
courses.description: Survey of the leading family systems models/theories, focusing on cultural responsiveness.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Systems of Family Counseling for Ánimo Emphasis
courses.description: Survey of the leading family systems models/theories, focusing on cultural responsiveness. Self-awareness, knowledge, interventions and social advocacy with Latinx clients for Ánimo Emphasis.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Groups: Process and Practice
courses.description: Basic issues and concepts related to group process. Demonstration of culturally informed group leadership skills, emphasizing self-reflection.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Practicum
courses.description: Supervised clinical practice with adults, families and children in approved community agencies. Practice in case management, documentation, use of community resources. Emphasizes dysfunction and health functioning. Hours accrued toward 280 required for yearlong practicum experience. Credit/No Credit only. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Practicum for Animo Emphasis
courses.description: Supervised clinical practice with adults, families and children, focusing on Latinx clients, in approved community agencies. Practice in case management, documentation, use of community resources. Emphasizes dysfunction and healthy functioning. Hours accrued towards 280 required for year-long practicum experience. Requires consent of Fieldwork Coordinator. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Addictions Counseling
courses.description: Etiology and treatment of addictive behaviors (e.g. substance abuse, gambling). Biological, psychological and systemic factors. Current approaches to assessment, intervention, prevention programs and relapse prevention, including Motivational Interviewing. Role of co-occurring disorders. Using community resources to help client and client's family. (COUN 535 and PSYC 535 are the same course).

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Crisis Intervention and Trauma Treatment
courses.description: Crisis theory and intervention, as well as basic aspects of theory and treatment of trauma experienced within diverse and multicultural contexts. Case management in the context of recovery orientation.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Appraisal in Counseling
courses.description: Theories and applications of psychological testing and other means of appraisal, as they relate to the practice of community-based counseling and marriage and family therapy.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Intimate Partner and Couples Counseling
courses.description: Treating intimate partners and couples, including overview of current theories, assessment, goal-setting, interventions, ethical issues and diversity issues. Assessing and treating intimate partner violence. Sexual dysfunctions and sex therapy. (COUN 562 and PSYC 562 are the same course)

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Advanced Practicum
courses.description: Advanced supervised clinical practice with adults, families and children in approved community agencies. Diagnosis, treatment planning, applied use of theory and techniques. Hours accrued toward 280 required for yearlong practicum experience. May be repeated once for credit.  Credit/No Credit only.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Advanced Practicum for Animo Emphasis
courses.description: Advanced supervised clinical practice with adults, families and children, focusing on Latinx clients, in approved community agencies. Emphasizes diagnosis, treatment planning, applied use of theory and techniques. Hours accrued towards 280 required for yearlong practicum experience. Credit/No Credit. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Advanced Practicum II
courses.description: On-campus supervision and instruction to students who completed the three-semester practicum requirement and still need to complete their 280 Direct Client Contact hours at their site. Conceptualization, advanced counseling skills, counselor processor and diversity. Credit/No Credit only.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Project
courses.description: Capstone program experience; taken final semester. Conduct original research relevant to the counseling field. Requires consent of faculty adviser.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Research and development in counseling pursued independently with periodic conference with instructor. May be repeated for a maximum of 3 units. Requires consent of instructor or graduate program adviser.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Introduction to Criminal Justice
courses.description: Overview of the criminal justice system. The historical and contemporary aspects of law, policing, courts and corrections from a social justice perspective.

sections.instructor: Amy Foust, Amy Foust, Amy Foust, Amy Foust

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Mythology of Crime and Justice
courses.description: Myths and misperceptions of crime, law and justice. How external influences shape perceptions of crime and perpetuate inequalities. Collateral consequences of crime myths.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Introduction to Criminal Courts
courses.description: Structure, operation and function of the U.S. criminal courts. Emphasizes pretrial and trial procedure, as well as the organizational roles, key players and behaviors within the court system.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Police and Society
courses.description: Critical overview of local policing from a historical and contemporary lens. Organizational structure, law and practices, including discretion, use of force and police-public interactions in a diverse society.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Introduction to Public Administration
courses.description: Introduces public administration through current trends and problems of public sector agencies in such areas as organization behavior, public budgeting, personnel, planning and policy making. Examples and cases from the Criminal Justice field. (POSC 320 and CRJU 320 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Leadership for Public Service
courses.description: Conceptions of leadership as applied in governmental and nonprofit sectors. Types of leaders; tools for leaders; leadership in public policy-making settings. Includes student project and extend leadership concepts; participation in CSUF Student Leadership Institute or similar activity. (POSC 322 and CRJU 322 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Juvenile Justice Administration
courses.description: Definitions of delinquency and the related responses of the interested institutions (police, courts and correction); the juvenile court (past and present), and prevention and correction programs (practicing and proposed).

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Victims of Crime
courses.description: Nature and extent of victimization in the population, risk factors and theories of victimization, consequences of victimization, types of victimization, as well as the social, political, and criminal justice system reaction and response to victims.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Theories of Crime and Delinquency
courses.description: Historical foundations and development of criminological theories to explain criminal behavior. Implications for criminal justice policy and practice.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Criminal Justice Research Methodology
courses.description: Introduction to basic techniques in criminal justice research; focus on literature review, correlation/causation, research design and sampling techniques. Read research reports and critically analyze research study methodology.

sections.instructor: Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Corrections
courses.description: Overview of the history and philosophies of corrections, emphasizing current trends and populations, policies and practices for adult correctional systems. The experience of individuals, from intake to reentry and its impacts on communities and society.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Immigration & Crime
courses.description: Analyzes the involvement of immigrants in crime through empirical studies and discusses the implications this has for public opinion and policy-governance.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Sex, Crime and Culture
courses.description: Rationale for law's concern with sexual conduct, developed via discussion of selected offenses and offenders. Lectures and guest speakers also present opposing perspectives regarding the role of law enforcement, courts and correction, research and reform.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Capital Punishment
courses.description: Issues relating to the use of capital punishment in the U.S., and arguments in support of and opposition to the death penalty. (CRJU 404 and POSC 404 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Restorative Justice
courses.description: Provides introductory knowledge and applications of restorative justice. Topics include values inherent in restorative justice, the purpose of restorative justice, various types of restorative justice, and the theoretical and practical underpinnings of restorative justice.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Policing the City
courses.description: Methods used by police to control crime and promote social order in inner city areas. Various issues from multiple perspectives (residents, merchants, customers, organizations and other users of public space).

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Mass Murder
courses.description: Incidence and prevalence of mass murder. Examine offender characteristics, theories and typologies. Threat assessment and prevention issues.

sections.instructor: Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos, Georgia Spiropoulos

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Human Resources Management
courses.description: Civil service and the merit system; recruitment procedures and examinations; position classification, salary structures, retirement plans, in-service training, employee organizations and personnel supervision. Examples and cases from the criminal justice field. Emphasizes themes and topics from criminal justice. (POSC 422 and CRJU 422 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Women and Crime
courses.description: Women as criminals and victims, gender differences in criminal behavior and the role of women as professionals in the criminal justice system. (CRJU 430 and GSS 430 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Controlling Crime
courses.description: Crime control and prevention. Common criminal justice tactics, such as imprisonment, capital punishment, camera surveillance, electronic monitoring, restorative justice, and situational crime prevention.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Correctional Rehabilitation
courses.description: Theories and techniques of correctional treatment. Current state of correctional rehabilitation with a focus on the What Works! literature and the value of proper programmatic evaluation and correctional classification.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Law, Punishment and Justice
courses.description: Theoretical scholarship in criminal justice is increasingly concerned with law in relation to delivery of justice and practices of punishment. Examines the rule of law, questions whether justice is different from law and reviews the role punishment plays.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Moot Court: Legal Practicum
courses.description: Open to undergraduates only. Prepares students for competition. Legal research, writing, court strategies and oral argument; civil liberties law, cases and adjudication; appellate court review and amicus brief reading and writing. May be repeated for a maximum of 12 units. (POSC 471 and CRJU 471 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Civil Liberties
courses.description: Constitutional rights and liberties as found in the Bill of Rights and the 14th Amendment, with particular attention to free speech, religious freedom, the right to bear arms, cruel and unusual punishment, and sexual privacy. (POSC 474 and CRJU 474 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Animals, Law and Society
courses.description: Behavioral and legal complexities of human-animal relationships. Individual and institutional harms to animals, the link between animal abuse and criminal violence, humane law enforcement and the challenge of securing justice for animals.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Courtroom Evidence
courses.description: Rules of evidence in the context of a criminal trial in a California court. Rules, their application and rationale. Lecture, discussion and simulated courtroom situations.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Criminal Law: Substantive
courses.description: History and evolution of criminal law from common law origins to present. Elements of crime, criminal offenses and defenses. Apply basic legal analysis.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Search, Seizure and Interrogation I
courses.description: Analyze laws that apply in common street search-and-seizure and interrogation situations in California; how they have evolved, and what developments are anticipated.

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Prelaw Internship
courses.description: Acquaints students with the legal profession. A supervised working commitment of eight hours weekly with an assigned individual or organization. May be repeated once for credit. (POSC 492 and CRJU 492 are the same course.)

courses.subject: CRJU
courses.title: Internships
courses.description: Criminal justice professions; eight to 20 hours per week as a supervised intern in a public agency or related organization. In addition to the job experience, interns meet in a weekly three-hour seminar. May be repeated once for credit. Requires consent of instructor.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Introduction to Dance
courses.description: Historical and contemporary dance forms. Experiences in various dance forms such as ballet, modern, jazz, folk, ethnic. Recommended for non-majors.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballet I
courses.description: Fundamental structure and technique of beginning classical ballet. May be taken for credit for a maximum of eight units. (2 hours activity per unit)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Contemporary Dance Practices I
courses.description: Fundamental structure and technique of beginning modern and/or contemporary dance styles. May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 8 units. (2 hours activity per unit)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance Improvisation
courses.description: Theory and practice of improvisation in movement. Practical use of improvisation in expressing imagery, developing choreographic concepts and enhancing performance. (4 hours activity)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Jazz I
courses.description: Modern jazz dance techniques and basic jazz choreography. May be taken for credit for a maximum of four units. (4 hours activity)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballet II
courses.description: Intermediate level technique of classical Ballet. May be taken for credit for a maximum of 4 units. (2 hours activity per unit)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Contemporary. Dance Practices II
courses.description: Intermediate-level technique of contemporary and modern dance styles. May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 8 units. (2 hours activity per unit)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Rhythmic Analysis
courses.description: Musical form and structure as it pertains to dance and choreography; musically notating dance rhythms and percussion accompaniment.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Jazz II
courses.description: Intermediate level skills in jazz technique and choreography. May be repeated for a maximum of four units. Requires consented placement test. (4 hours activity)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Tap Dance II
courses.description: Intermediate skills in tap technique and choreography. May be repeated for up to four units. Requires consented placement test. (2 hours activity per unit)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance and Cultural Diversity
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Impact of various dance forms, from primitive time to modern, on diverse cultures. Contributions of immigrants, minorities and women to dance as a personal, social and cultural expression.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballet III
courses.description: Classical ballet technique at the second stage of the intermediate level. Complex combinations. Elements of technique and theory. May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 6 units. (2 hours activity per unit)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Contemporary Dance Practices III
courses.description: Contemporary and/or modern dance technique at an advanced intermediate level. Technical theory with emphasis on more complex combinations. May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 8 units. (2 hours activity per unit)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance Composition
courses.description: Choreography and forms of beginning dance composition. Final project required. (6 hours activity)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Forces and Figures in Dance
courses.description: Dance history from primitive to contemporary times, including historical eras, famous dancers, choreographers and companies.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance Theory and Criticism
courses.description: Dance theory and philosophy, choreographic styles, published reviews, critique writing. Fulfills the course requirement for the university upper-division baccalaureate writing requirement for dance majors.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Mindful Conditioning for Performers
courses.description: Principles of mindfulness and conditioning as they relate to performers. In-class and outside assignments; create routines. May include, but not limited to breathing techniques, meditation techniques, cardio routines, GYROKINESIS®, Pilates, yoga and journaling.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance for Musical Theatre
courses.description: Musical theatre dance techniques. Ensemble work and individual approaches to style, synthesizing and building upon the foundations of ballet, jazz, modern and lyrical dance. May be repeated once for credit. (6 hours activity)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Contemporary Dance Practices IV
courses.description: Advanced level skills in contemporary and/or modern dance. Emphasize individual techniques. May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 9 units.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Advanced Dance Composition
courses.description: Elements and forms in dance composition. Choreographing dances of concert quality. (6 hours activity)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Creative Dance for Children
courses.description: Methods and materials for teaching creative dance to children.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Performance
courses.description: Performing in stage or camera productions. May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 10 units. (more than 6 hours activity).  (THTR 478A and DANC 478A are the same course.)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Repertory and Performance Techniques
courses.description: Broadens understanding of the history, theory and practice of concert dance performance. Emphasizes learning repertory and exploring performance techniques. May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 6 units. Requires audition. (4 hours activity)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Production and Performance Projects in Dance
courses.description: Projects that culminate in production or performance. May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Undergraduate research projects. May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: The Economic Environment
courses.description: Application of economics to the problems of unemployment and inflation, the distribution of income, competition and monopoly, the role of government in the economy, other policy issues.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Principles of Microeconomics
courses.description: Principles of individual consumer and producer decision-making in various market structures, the price system, market performance and government policy.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
courses.description: Principles of macroeconomics analysis and policy, unemployment and inflation, financial institutions, international trade, economic growth, comparative systems.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics, Causality, and Analytics
courses.description: Modern economic analysis, which centers around causal inference - how X causes Y. How economists and social scientists identify causal effects without experiments, how to diagram causality and how to implement casual methods using R.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomic Analysis
courses.description: Rational decision-making behavior of consumers and firms, price and output determination in markets. Primarily for economics majors, but open to all students who qualify. May not receive credit for both ECON 310 and ECON 315

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Business Microeconomics
courses.description: Business decisions in alternative market structures with special emphasis on problem solving in a business context using economic concepts and methods. Not open to economics majors. May not receive credit for both ECON 310 and ECON 315.

sections.instructor: Suprea Sandhu, Suprea Sandhu, Suprea Sandhu, Suprea Sandhu
Denise Stanley, Denise Stanley, Denise Stanley, Denise Stanley
Denise Stanley, Denise Stanley, Denise Stanley, Denise Stanley

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Macroeconomic Analysis
courses.description: Macroeconomic analysis of policy and events in the short and long run, and of the open economy. Sources and interpretation of macroeconomic data. May not receive credit for both ECON 320 and ECON 325.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Macroeconomic Theory
courses.description: Macroeconomic theory and models of national income, employment, prices, fiscal and monetary policy, and the open economy. Analysis of business cycles and long run economic growth. May not receive credit for both ECON 320 and ECON 325.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Comparative Economic Systems
courses.description: Why do some nations fail and some succeed in a transforming global landscape? Compare and contrast socioeconomic systems around the world. Explore the origins of power, institutions, incentives, allocation mechanisms and ownership of means of production.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economies of the Pacific Rim
courses.description: Dimensions of industrialization, agriculture, investment, human resources and trade in economies of the Far East (including Japan and China), India and related nations of the Pacific Rim.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economic Development: Analysis and Case Studies
courses.description: Processes of economic growth with references to developing areas. Capital formation, resource allocation, relation to the world economy, economic planning and institutional factors, with case studies.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: The International Economy
courses.description: Theory, practice and institutions of the international economy. International trade and investment, effects of trade policies, trade blocs, balance of payments, foreign exchange markets, short-run and long-run determinants of exchange rates.

sections.instructor: Huiran Pan, Huiran Pan, Huiran Pan
Huiran Pan, Huiran Pan, Huiran Pan

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economies of the Middle East
courses.description: What drives economic growth in the Middle East? Topics include oil dependency, demographic shifts, investment in human capital, transition from command to market economies, governance, state capacity and regional integration.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economic Research Methods
courses.description: Basics of applied economic research. How to access existing economic knowledge, locate and compile economic data, and analyze economic problems using theory and quantitative methods.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Econometrics
courses.description: Economic measurement: specification and estimation of econometric models; statistical methods in economic research.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Economics
courses.description: Economic theory from microeconomics and macroeconomics. Content varies; constrained optimization problems and rational decision-making.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Data Science for Economics and Policy Analysis
courses.description: Hands-on introduction to employing big data to solve economic and social problems. Studies modern applied economic approaches for quantitative social science research and policy analysis. Real-world projects develop skills for all steps in the data science pipeline.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics Capstone
courses.description: Taken in the last semester of studies. Students demonstrate proficiency in economic theory and quantitative methods and the ability to apply those to economic issues, including analyzing news reports, summarizing scholarly journal articles, writing policy and/or conducting original research.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: Planned and supervised work experience. Credit/No Credit only. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Requires consent of the department internship adviser and one semester in residence at the university.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Directed independent inquiry. May be repeated for a maximum of 3 units. Not open to students on academic probation. Requires consent of department chair.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Advanced Macroeconometrics: Time Series and Forecasting
courses.description: Advanced estimation techniques of macroeconomic data. Economic forecasting. Time series econometrics. Stationarity and unit roots. Deterministic and stochastic processes. Vector Autoregressive Analysis. Macroeconomic applications. Use of econometric and statistical computer softwares.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Macroeconomic Perspective for Managers
courses.description: National income, inflation and unemployment. Short run economic fluctuations and business cycles. Monetary and fiscal policy. The financial system and financial crises. Open economy, the exchange rate and the trade balance. Macroeconomic policy making. Economic forecasting using macroeconomic indicators. Not open to Economics graduate students or students with credit for ECON 320 or ECON 325.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Transportation Economics
courses.description: Analyze urban transportation and public policy using microeconomic theory, constrained optimization, econometrics and data analytics. Topics include: travel demand modeling; transportation costs; congestion and other transportation-related externalities; land use and its effects on transportation; econometric models used in transportation contexts.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Current Research in Economics
courses.description: Read, present and replicate scholarly research published in peer-reviewed journals covering a variety of topics in economics. Receive guidance as to research methodology, composing a research paper and professional presentation. Attendance at departmental research seminars required.

courses.subject: EDD
courses.title: Inquiry III
courses.description: Applying the philosophical and epistemological foundations of educational research to the design of a formal research project. Draws upon educational research and the methods using a mixed-methods orientation that includes quantitative and qualitative perspectives.

courses.subject: EDD
courses.title: Higher Education, Community College Systems, Structures, and Cultures
courses.description: Higher education, from Egyptian Era to the diversity of current postsecondary instructions, philosophies and orientations. Organizational development and structures of higher educational systems and the impact of faculty, student and administrative cultures on higher education leaders.

courses.subject: EDD
courses.title: Human Dimensions of Educational Change
courses.description: Issues associated with change. Change as a sociopolitical process; sources and purpose of change; coping with multiple reform efforts; decision-making processes; reform implementation; problems of resistance to change in curriculum and instruction; and change as a continuous process.

courses.subject: EDD
courses.title: Student Learning and Development
courses.description: Student development and learning theories based on cognitive, psychosocial, typology and person-environment perspectives. Role of faculty and others in the collaborative development and implementation of responsive curricula and co-curricula at two- and four-year institutions.

courses.subject: EDD
courses.title: Epistemology, History and Structure of Contemporary Education
courses.description: Epistemological and historical trends that have shaped the structure of contemporary education. Influence of major schools of thought, including rationalism, empiricism, pragmatism, behaviorism and constructivism; and how modern education structure, curriculum and pedagogy have been influenced by these various perspectives.

courses.subject: EDD
courses.title: Linking Research to Problems of Practice
courses.description: Identifying complex problems of educational practice appropriate for doctoral research. Small-group instruction provides coaching that enables students to initiate the research cycle by linking research to problems of practices.

courses.subject: EDD
courses.title: Refining Research Questions
courses.description: Further refine research questions or hypotheses, select the research method to investigate the research question, design a research study that specifies methods to be implemented for data collection and analysis.

courses.subject: EDD
courses.title: Seminar in Educational Research Design and Implementation
courses.description: Assists in designing, completing and defending a scholarly dissertation research study. Develop intended measurable outcomes and establish methods, timetables and specific deliverables for the completion of those outcomes in consultation with the course instructor. May be repeated for a maximum of 12 units. Requires consent of program director or graduate advisor.

courses.subject: EDD
courses.title: Dissertation Research
courses.description: Individual research on a dissertation. Conferences with a faculty adviser and committee members, culminating in the publication of a dissertation. May be repeated for a maximum of 12 units.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent doctoral level inquiry for qualified students.

sections.instructor: Daniel Choi, Maritza Lozano, Allan Mucerino, Marc Ecker
Christopher Newman, Michelle Garcia, Deniz Fierro, Eric Rabitoy

courses.subject: EDAD
courses.title: Clear Administrative Services Credential Program (CASC): Coaching
courses.description: A job-embedded induction program providing opportunities to widen expertise in school leadership. The supervisory coaching component taken with either the EDAD 501 content series or in conjunction with the EDD curriculum. Satisfies the coaching requirement for students working on their CASC.

courses.subject: EDAD
courses.title: Organizational Leadership and Management B
courses.description: Use organizational theory and leadership studies to understand and bring about change in schools. Organization, structure and cultural context of schools, and study techniques used to develop, build consensus, lead others and implement shared vision and goals.

sections.instructor: Jennifer Goldstein, Jennifer Goldstein, Jennifer Goldstein, Jennifer Goldstein

courses.subject: EDAD
courses.title: P-12 Instructional Leadership and Assessment A
courses.description: Approaches for advocating, nurturing and sustaining a school culture and instructional program conducive to student learning and professional growth.

sections.instructor: George Herrera, George Herrera, George Herrera, George Herrera

courses.subject: EDAD
courses.title: Instructional Leadership in Higher Education
courses.description: Instructional leadership in higher educational settings and the role of the student development educator in advocating, nurturing and sustaining a culture that supports student learning and development.

courses.subject: EDAD
courses.title: Instructional Leadership and Assessment B
geCategories:
Satisfies Graduate Writing Requirement
Free Course Material
courses.description: Use data and inquiry methods to assess students' learning and instructional practices. Apply data analysis to determine interventions and assess impact.

courses.subject: EDAD
courses.title: Foundations of Leadership through Equity in P-12 Schools
courses.description: This course will introduce conceptual underpinnings of program and examine theoretical frameworks and research methods that help school leaders promote just and equitable education for all students.

sections.instructor: Rodolfo Acosta, Rodolfo Acosta, Rodolfo Acosta, Rodolfo Acosta

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Electric Circuits
courses.description: Units; Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws; mesh and nodal analysis, superposition; Thevenin and Norton theorems; RL and RC transients; phasors and steady state sinusoidal analysis; response as a function of frequency; current, voltage and power relationships; polyphase circuits.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Electric Circuits Laboratory
courses.description: Simple resistive RL and RC circuits, electrical measurement techniques, verification of basic circuit laws through hard-wired breadboarding and CAD circuit simulation. (3 hours laboratory)

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Computer Logic and Architecture
courses.description: Logic design and organization of the major components of a computer, analysis and synthesis of combinational and sequential logics, analysis of the arithmetic, memory control and I/O units, concepts in computer control.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Computer Logic and Architecture Lab
