courses.description: Computer-Aided Design (CAD) of digital logic circuits, including decoders, multiplexes, adders and subtracters, counters, shift registers and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) of a computer. After verifying the CAD design through simulation, the circuits are built on a protoboard. (3 hours laboratory)

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Microcontrollers
courses.description: Microcontrollers, microcontroller programming model and instruction set, assembler directives, writing and debugging microcontroller assembly language routines, microcontroller memory system, microcontroller communication systems. (1 hour lecture, 4 hours laboratory)

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Electronics
courses.description: Characteristics and elementary applications of semiconductor diodes, field-effect transistors and bipolar-junction transistors and operational amplifiers; mid-frequency small-signal analysis and design of transistors.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Engineering Analysis
courses.description: Fundamentals and engineering applications of Fourier transforms, Laplace transforms, complex analysis, vector analysis; engineering applications. (EGCE 308, EGEC 308, EGGN 308 and EGME 308 are the same course.)

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Network Analysis
courses.description: Performance of RLC circuits; complex frequency and the s-plane; frequency response and resonance; network topology; two-port network characterization; classical filter theory.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Electronic Circuits
courses.description: Continuation of EGEC 303; analyzing and designing multistage and feedback amplifiers; frequency characteristics of amplifiers, frequency characteristics and stability of feedback amplifiers, differential amplifiers, design of IC circuit biasing, operational amplifiers and their applications.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Electronic Circuits Lab
courses.description: Computer-Aided Design (CAD) of electronic circuits, including multi-stage feedback amplifiers; linear and integrated circuits; ADC and DAC and wireless design projects. After verifying the CAD design through simulation, the circuits are built on a protoboard. (3 hours laboratory)

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Introduction to Electromechanics
courses.description: Electromagnetic fields and circuits; transformers, saturation effects. Simple electro-mechanical systems. Circuit models, terminal characteristics and applications of DC and AC machines.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Modeling and Simulation of Signals and Systems
courses.description: Modeling and simulation of physical systems, mathematical description of systems, transfer functions, poles and zeros, frequency response, continuous and discrete-time convolution, continuous and discrete Fourier transforms, Laplace and Z transforms, Fast Fourier Transforms, simulation using Matlab.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Computer Design and Organization
courses.description: Computer system, central processing unit (CPU) organization and design, instruction set and addressing modes, microprogrammed control unit design, cache memory, internal memory, virtual memory, input/output interfacing, parallel processors, superscalar processors (2 hours lecture, 4 hours laboratory).

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Engineering Economics and Professionalism
courses.description: Development, evaluation and presentation of design alternatives for engineering systems and projects using principles of engineering economy and cost benefit analysis. Engineering profession, professional ethics and related topics. (Not available for use on graduate study plans.) (EGEC 401, EGCE 401, and EGME 401 are the same course.)

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Introduction to Linear Systems
courses.description: Development of time and frequency domain models for physical systems. Linearization process and representation with block diagrams and signal flow graphs; discrete-time systems and digital signals including use of Z-transforms; stability theory of continuous and discrete time systems.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Electro-Optical Systems
courses.description: Introduction to electro-optics; optical radiation characteristics and sources; geometrical and physical optics; lasers and electro-optical modulation; quantum and thermal optical radiation detectors; detector performance analysis; electro-optical systems modeling and analysis; application examples.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Feedback Control Systems
courses.description: Feedback control system characteristics; stability in the frequency and time domains; analysis and design of continuous-time systems using root-locus, Bode and Nyquist plots, Nichols chart and applications.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Electronic Circuits
courses.description: Power amplifiers and tuned amplifiers; RF amplifiers; modulation and detection circuits; oscillators; and operational amplifier applications.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Advanced Digital Design using Verilog HDL
courses.description: Fundamentals of Verilog programming; behavioral modeling using Verilog; structural modeling using Verilog; RTL design using Verilog; Shannon's decomposition; FPGA architecture; Digital design, synthesis and implementation using FPGA.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Electrical Engineering Design Projects Laboratory
courses.description: Practical aspects of design and project construction. Instructor-approved design project in electrical engineering, inter-disciplinary projects. Using CAD program for schematic capture and simulation. Constructing final hardware according to the design specification. Performance evaluation and demonstration of project. (1 hour lecture, 6 hours laboratory).

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Directed independent design project. May be taken for credit for a maximum of six units. Requires consent of adviser and instructor.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Specialized topics in engineering selected in consultation with and completed under the supervision of the instructor. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Requires approval of study plan by adviser.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: CMOS VLSI Design
courses.description: Surface physics of MOS system and MOS device physics. Short channel effect; hot carrier effect, subthreshold conduction. CMOS fabrication process. Layout design rules. Scaling design and analysis of CMOS circuits. Standard cell method. CAD design and SPICE simulation.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Computer Arithmetic Structures
courses.description: Suitability of signed binary number systems for high-speed arithmetic, normalized and denormalized binary floating-point representation formats, high-speed algorithms, implementations and design tradeoffs for fast arithmetic operations - addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, floating point arithmetic.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Real-Time Audio and Language Processing
courses.description: Introduction to designing, developing and implementing audio and language processing algorithms, in real time, on dedicated processors.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Analysis of Random Signals
courses.description: Random processes pertinent to communications, controls and other physical applications, Markov sequences and processes, the orthogonality principle.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Project
courses.description: Project proposal must be approved prior to last day of class instruction of the preceding semester. Requires classified graduate status; consent of graduate program adviser and program coordinator.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: Unless approved by the department chair, EGEC 598 cannot be taken if EGEC 597 has been completed. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Requires consent of adviser. Classified graduate students only.

courses.subject: EGEC
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: Unless approved by department chair, EGEC 599 cannot be taken if EGEC 597 has been completed. May be repeated for a maximum of six units. Requires consent of adviser.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: The Teaching Experience: Exploration
courses.description: Roles, responsibilities and impact of educators, while examining how schools can both advance and hinder equity. Engage with culturally responsive and antiracist practices in schools and education. Requires 10 hours of observation. (EDSC 110, EDEL 110 and SPED 110 are the same course.)

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Introduction to Elementary Classroom Teaching
courses.description: Exploratory course with field assignments for those considering careers in schools, grades TK-8. Students taking this course to meet the prerequisite for the Multiple Subject Credential Program must earn a "C-" or better. Fieldwork required.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Cultural Pluralism in Elementary Schools
courses.description: Culture and cultural pluralism in grades TK-8. Examine one's own beliefs and values; classroom practices and materials that promote equity; strategies for learning about students; history/traditions of cultural groups; and assess multicultural education programs. Students taking this course to meet the prerequisite for either the Multiple Subject or the Special Education Credential Program must earn a "C-" or better.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Integrated Curriculum and Instruction in the Elementary School
courses.description: Additional study of elementary curriculum emphasizing language arts, integrated instruction across the curriculum and assessing learning outcomes. Must be taken for a letter grade if enrolled in the credential program. A "B" or better is required to pass the course.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Foundations in Elementary School Teaching
courses.description: Elementary curriculum, instructional planning and principles of effective teaching. Integrate workforce connections by introducing professional guest speakers and career-oriented panels, enhancing understanding of effective instructional strategies and classroom management. Contemporary and legal issues in education.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Language Arts and Reading Instruction in the Public Schools
courses.description: Overview of principles of reading instruction, elements of the language arts program including literature-based reading, content area reading, the role of phonics, emergent literacy and diagnosis of reading problems. Must be taken Credit/No Credit. A "B" (3.0) or better is required to receive a grade of credit.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Methods and Inquiry for Teaching English Learners
courses.description: Theoretical foundations, legal issues and school programs for the education of English learners. Assessment, materials, methods and strategies for English language development and learning across the curriculum for elementary school English learners. Must be taken Credit/No Credit. A "B" (3.0) or better is required to receive a grade of Credit.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Mathematics Curriculum and Instruction in Elementary School Teaching
courses.description: Instructional materials, learning styles, inquiry, concept learning, problem solving, various instructional strategies applied to teaching of mathematics in TK through 8th grade. Must be taken Credit/No Credit. A "B" (3.0) or better is required to receive a grade of credit.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Science Curriculum and Instruction in Elementary School Teaching
courses.description: Instructional materials, learning styles, inquiry, concept learning, problem solving, various instructional strategies applied to the teaching of science in TK through 8th grade. Must be taken Credit/No Credit. A "B" (3.0) or better is required to receive a grade of credit.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Social Studies Curriculum and Instruction in Elementary School Teaching
courses.description: Instructional materials, learning styles, inquiry, concept learning, problem solving, various instructional strategies applied to teaching social studies. Credit/No Credit only. A "B" (3.0) or better is required to receive a grade of credit.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Supervised Fieldwork in Elementary Teacher Education
courses.description: Students serve as teacher participants in an assigned elementary school classroom. Credit/No Credit only. A "B" or better is required to receive a grade of credit. May be repeated for a maximum of 2 units.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Student Teaching in the Elementary School
courses.description: Participate in a regular elementary school teaching program for the full school day. Credit/ No Credit only. A "B" (3.0) or better is required to receive a grade of credit. May be repeated for a maximum of 15 units.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Visual and Performing Arts Methods: Art, Dance, Drama and Music
courses.description: Instructional materials, learning styles, integration and strategies as they apply to teaching the arts in elementary education. Credit/No Credit only. A "B" (3.0) or better is required to receive a grade of credit.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: Community, School, and Classroom Issues
courses.description: Current issues of elementary school teaching, including classroom management, parent-teacher communication, school law and child abuse reporting. Credit/No Credit only. A "B" (3.0) or better is required to receive a grade of credit.

courses.subject: EDEL
courses.title: P.E., Health and Mainstreaming Education
courses.description: Mainstreaming students with special needs, health education and physical education in elementary school settings. Credit/No Credit only. A "B" (3.0) or better is required to receive a grade of credit.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Beginning College Writing
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of expository prose. Grammatical and basic rhetorical concepts and practices necessary for successful college writing. Placement to be determined by multiple measures. Instructional fee.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Preparatory College Writing
courses.description: Practice and instruction in college-level writing. Writing, revision, grammar, rhetorical and research skills necessary for success in ENGL 101. Enrollment determined by appropriate placement assessment. (ENGL 101P and ESE 101P are the same course.)

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to Creative Writing
courses.description: Exploratory creative writing with the opportunity to write in various genres. No credit toward the major or minor.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Literature and Popular Culture
courses.description: For non-English majors who like to read. Uses subjects in popular culture to study fiction, drama and poetry; including non-conformity and rebellion in modern music, conspiracy theory, visual literacy and the influence of science.  Carries no credit toward the major.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: British Literature to 1760
courses.description: Major periods and movements, major authors and major forms through 1760.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: British Literature from 1760
courses.description: Major periods and movements, major authors and major forms from 1760 through modern times.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Analysis of Literary Forms
courses.description: Main literary forms-prose fiction, poetry and drama-are studied and analyzed. English majors should schedule this basic course as early as possible.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Advanced College Writing
courses.description: Writing expository prose for non-English majors. Precision in rhetoric and development of individual style by concentration on matters of diction, audience, emphasis and persuasion.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: The Structure of Modern English
courses.description: Grammar of contemporary English. Modern English usage. Requirement for application to English Teaching Credential.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Advanced College Writing for English Studies
courses.description: Interpretive frameworks of communities within the discipline of English Studies (literary studies, creative writing, English education, composition, cultural criticism). Uses discursive conventions of these communities to produce formal and informal texts of various genres. Requires completion of all lower-division writing requirements.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Shakespeare
courses.description: Study of the major plays.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Shakespeare on Film
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Analyze representative Shakespeare plays; view and analyze film versions of each play. Use literary and film terminology to write critical responses to drama and film, develop storyboards and conceptualize a Shakespeare play adaptation "pitch" with set, costume design, marketing strategy. (ENGL 331 and THTR 331 are the same course.)

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Children's Literature
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: World literature written primarily for children, including material from the oral tradition, realistic fiction, fantasy and poetry.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Legal Writing
courses.description: Advanced composition stressing logic, reasoning and legal analysis.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Theories of Response to Written Composition
courses.description: Theories and practices in tutoring writing. Prepares students to work with writers from diverse backgrounds and disciplines. May be taken for letter grade or Credit/No credit.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Tutor Supervision
courses.description: May be taken for letter grade or Credit/No credit.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Advanced Creative Writing
courses.description: Instruction and practice in a workshop setting for students with some experience in creative writing; emphasizes writing for professional markets. Consult the class schedule to determine section's emphasis. May be repeated once with different topic.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Language and Power in African American Culture
courses.description: Language use within the African American community. Topics include language history, dialect vs. language, communicative practices, language in education policy, language and ideology, and language attitudes. (ENGL 410 and AFAM 410 are the same course.)

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Restoration and 18th-Century Literature
courses.description: Major writers from prose, poetry and dramatic genres, such as Butler, Rochester, Dryden, Pepys, Swift, Addison and Steele, Pope, Boswell, Johnson, Sheridan, Wycherly and Gay, as well as selected minor writers.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to Graduate Studies in English
courses.description: Research techniques, analytical approaches and theories of literature. Basic orientation in graduate literary studies.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Creative Writing Workshop
courses.description: Intensive graduate-level workshop in creative writing. Produce own work, write critiques of others' works and discuss opportunities for publication. May focus on writing poetry or fiction or a mix of fiction and drama, depending on instructor's expertise. Each topic may be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Graduate Seminar: Major Writers
courses.description: As appropriate to the specialized research and publication of instructor; major figures such as Shakespeare, Dante, Cervantes, Goethe, Bronte, Twain, Joyce, Woolf and Morrison. May be repeated with different topics for a maximum of 9 units.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Graduate Seminar: Literary Genres
courses.description: As appropriate to the specialized research and publication of instructor, major literary types such as the epic, novel, short story, lyric poetry, tragedy, comedy and historical drama. May be repeated once for credit with a different topic.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Writing Theory and Practice for Teaching Associates
courses.description: Theory and practice of the composing process for the beginning college teacher of expository writing. Required of all English Department Teaching Associates during their first semester of teaching. Requires admission to the English Department Teaching Associate Program.

courses.subject: ENED
courses.title: Teaching English in the Secondary School
courses.description: Principles, methods and materials of teaching English in the secondary school. Students must earn a "B-" (2.7) or better to meet the requirements for earning a preliminary Single Subject credential.

courses.subject: ENST
courses.title: Sustainability Projects
courses.description: Interdisciplinary teams work on real world problems related to sustainability on campus or in the community. (ENST 492 and CHEM 492 are the same course.)

courses.subject: ENST
courses.title: Sustainability Internship
courses.description: Field experience in a sustainability related career.

courses.subject: ENST
courses.title: Environmental Issues and Approaches
courses.description: Interdisciplinary approaches to environmental problems and research methods. Prepare seminars and papers on research design for potential thesis topics. Meets graduate writing requirement.

courses.subject: ENST
courses.title: Environmental Evaluation and Protection
courses.description: Environmental parameters (water, air, solid wastes, noise, radiation, etc.). Techniques in monitoring and measurement; effect on human health; environmental quality standards and controls. Demonstrations and field trips.

courses.subject: ENST
courses.title: Selected Topics in Environmental Problems
courses.description: Various environmental topics, contemporary or historic, that focus on problems (e.g., law, endangered habitats, planning, global environmental issues, etc.). Topic chosen and outline will be circulated prior to registration. May be repeated with different topics for a maximum of 18 units.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Personal Financial Management
courses.description: Financial problems of the household in allocating resources and planning expenditures. Housing, insurance, installment buying, medical care, savings and investments. Special financial planning problems faced by minorities and women. May not be used to fulfill the concentration requirement in finance.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Financial Management I
courses.description: Financial statement analysis. Interest rates and valuing cash flows (TVM; valuing stocks and bonds). Investment decision rules and capital budgeting. Risk and return (CAPM) and cost of capital.

sections.instructor: Erdem Ucar, Erdem Ucar, Erdem Ucar
Yuming Li, Yuming Li, Yuming Li

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Financial Management II
courses.description: Brief review of risk/return and capital budgeting. Firm valuation, long-term financing, capital structure, payout policy and financial forecasting, focusing on valuation. Integrate data analytics to provide a hands-on approach to valuation and financial policies.

sections.instructor: Md Noman Hossain, Md Noman Hossain

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Working Capital Management and Computer Applications
courses.description: Analyze working capital management and policy, liquidity measurement, sources of financing for periods of cash deficits; manage accounts receivable and inventories; financial forecasting and short-term financing.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Financial Analysis for Investors and Lenders
courses.description: Interpretation of financial statement from the perspective of the financial analyst and creditor. Economic meaning of financial statement data for the purpose of evaluating a company's financial performance.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Introduction to Investments
courses.description: Institutional characteristics of securities markets, security valuation, fundamental and technical analysis, modern portfolio theory and mean-variance analysis, capital asset pricing model, market efficiency, options, portfolio analysis and investment funds. Apply data analytics to investment problems.

sections.instructor: Arsenio Staer, Arsenio Staer, Arsenio Staer
James Primbs, James Primbs, James Primbs
Ajay Bhootra, Ajay Bhootra, Ajay Bhootra
Shane Kim, Shane Kim, Shane Kim

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Student Managed Investment Fund
courses.description: Manage a portfolio of stocks and bonds funded by an external or internal sponsor. Investment teams may compete against local universities for the opportunity to invest funds for a sponsor organization.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Capital and Money Markets
courses.description: Capital and money markets in the American and international economies; markets for new corporate and government issues; secondary markets; use of derivative securities for hedging; factors influencing yields and security prices.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Real Estate Principles
courses.description: Real estate principles, practices and investment decisions. Equity investment, finance, legal aspects, practices, principles, property development, real estate administration in the public sector, real estate market analysis and valuation.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Real Estate Investment Analysis
courses.description: Alternative analytical techniques in evaluating real estate investments. Tax aspects, measurement of investment returns, application of computer models to investment decisions. Lecture, discussion and case analysis of major investment types - raw land, apartment houses, commercial and industrial uses.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Principles of Risk Management and Insurance
courses.description: Analysis of the risk management process, introduction to property and liability insurance, employee benefits and financial planning. Overview of the insurance industry and insurance problems.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: International Business Finance
courses.description: Financing problems of the multinational business. International financial environment, taxation of foreign income, the cost of capital in international capital and money markets, problems of risk in foreign investments, and financial techniques for the operation of the multinational firm.

sections.instructor: Arsenio Staer, Arsenio Staer, Arsenio Staer
Amadeu Dasilva, Amadeu Dasilva, Amadeu Dasilva
Amadeu Dasilva, Amadeu Dasilva, Amadeu Dasilva

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Global Risk Management and International Finance
courses.description: Loss control within the field of global insurance and risk management to provide  knowledge for the practical application of international financial risk management principles techniques and methods utilized in multinational corporations and governmental organizations operations.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Estate Planning
courses.description: Estate planning from the perspective of a Certified Financial Planner practitioner. Required in order to take the CFP® Certification Examination. Considerable discussion of federal legislation controlling estate planning.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Quantitative Theory of Interest
courses.description: The theory of interest in both finite and continuous time; the use of various annuity functions as a basis for reserving, valuation, pricing, duration, asset/liability management, amortization schedules and measurement of fund performance; term structure of interest rates.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Commercial Bank and Financial Institution Management
courses.description: Financial institution problem solutions. Major financial intermediaries and the decision-making problems they face. Regulation and its effect on management operations. Group problems and case studies.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Financial Forecasting and Budgeting
courses.description: Forecasting in financial management; profit planning and control process; goals, technical procedures and effects of budgeting; mechanics of forecasting and budgeting, follow-up and control.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Capital Markets and Fixed Income Analysis
courses.description: Fixed income markets, including the price dynamics and risk profiles of various fixed-income securities, derivatives, yields, duration, credit analysis of bonds, portfolio management strategies, calculating performance and identifying factors driving fixed-income returns.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Business Valuation, Mergers and Acquisitions
courses.description: Valuation, especially for mergers and acquisitions. Valuation methods and their application in mergers and acquisitions. May not receive credit for both FIN 440 and FIN 540.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Advanced Security Analysis for Bonds
courses.description: Integrate portfolio management techniques from FIN 442 with advanced analysis of fixed income securities to achieve a desired investment objective. Use market data platforms such as FactSet and Bloomberg to combine macroeconomics with company-specific factors to develop high-conviction investment recommendations.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Options and Futures
courses.description: Put and call options, option pricing theory and models. Financial futures pricing, hedging strategies and models. Institutional characteristics of futures trading. Options and futures on stock indices. Options on futures, theoretical relationship between options and futures.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Real Estate Practice
courses.description: Professional aspects of real estate business, overview of the real estate industry, ethics, licensing, contracts, forms, disclosure documents, listing properties, handling offers, closing sales transactions; financing, escrow, title and taxation issues; and 1031 exchanges requirements for investment property.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: A supervised experience where financial principles or methods are applied in a fieldwork setting.  Mandatory class meetings for students to discuss their experience and integrate financial practice.  Sections for other concentrations within the department will include  application of relevant principles. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Managerial Finance
courses.description: Modern theory and practice of financial management. Net present value and the time value of money. Basic principles of risk and return. Capital budgeting and forecasting. Capital structure and dividend theory. Firm valuation from a value-based management and corporate governance perspective.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)
courses.description: ERM framework with the integration of pure, financial, strategic and operational risks. Discusses seven building blocks for developing an ERM program. Legal and regulatory environment, technical tools and future prediction on ERM.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Not open to students on academic probation. Requires consent of instructor, approval by department chair and associate dean.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Fundamental French-A
courses.description: Introduces essentials of the French language: fundamental vocabulary and grammatical structures. Conversational and reading/writing skills are equally stressed, and relevant cultural aspects are considered. Conducted in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Fundamental French-B
courses.description: Continuation of systematic introduction of fundamental vocabulary and grammatical structures. Maintains equal emphasis on speaking and reading/writing skills, along with the study of French culture. Conducted in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Explorations in Literature
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Promotes deeper understanding and appreciation of French literary texts. Each genre (narrative, dramatic, poetic) introduces great writers. In-depth study of selected works initiates students to critical modes of reading and tools for literary analysis. Conducted in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Techniques of French-English Translation
courses.description: Overview of theories of translation; examines several types and examples of translation (technical to literary). Actual translation from English to French and French to English.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Topics in French/Francophone Culture
courses.description: Different "texts" (cinema, the media, internet, literature, art) centered around cultural topics (e.g., "City and Country," "The Outsider"). Tools to understand French-speaking culture(s), from recent social issues to classic art and literature. Course may be repeated with different topics for a maximum of 9 units. Conducted in French.

courses.subject: GSS
courses.title: Decoding Desire: Gender and Sexuality in the Humanities
courses.description: Gender representation in the humanities, using primary texts from around the world that shape global perspectives on the human condition. Rationality, the moral dimensions of individuals and communities, and the social construction of gender.

courses.subject: GSS
courses.title: Introduction to Queer Studies
courses.description: Introduces the field of Queer Studies by examining foundational theoretical texts, contemporary scholarship, and cultural productions that address questions concerning power, desire, sex, politics, bodies, nationalism, citizenship, transnationalism, and race.

courses.subject: GSS
courses.title: Digital Culture, Gender and Sexuality
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Current technologies and their relationship to gender issues, combining theoretical considerations with practical applications. Learn some basic technologies to use as tools for projects.

courses.subject: GSS
courses.title: Thinking and Writing: Methods to Change the World
courses.description: Study and evaluate various methodological approaches used to address gender issues, such as survey analysis, oral history, personal narrative and ethnography. Develop research skills. Develop writing skills, including proposals and research papers.

courses.subject: GSS
courses.title: Politics of Sexuality
courses.description: Cultural politics of sexuality within the U.S. and across national and cultural boundaries using feminist theories and methods. A focus on sexual controversies illuminates the relationship between sex, power and social change.

courses.subject: GSS
courses.title: Women and Crime
courses.description: Women as criminals and victims, gender differences in criminal behavior and the role of women as professionals in the criminal justice system. (CRJU 430 and GSS 430 are the same course.)

courses.subject: GSS
courses.title: Internship and Community Service
courses.description: Internship with guided tutorial in community organizations. Focus on gender and women's issues in a feminist framework.

courses.subject: GSS
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Conduct extended research in Women's Studies, or link an interest in another discipline to an interest in Women's Studies. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Requires approval by instructor teaching a Women's Studies class, or by Chair of Women and Gender Studies.

courses.subject: EGGN
courses.title: Introduction to Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to engineering disciplines and their sub-fields, basic tools used in engineering practice, hands-on engineering projects.

courses.subject: EGGN
courses.title: Computer Methods in Numerical Analysis
courses.description: Use of numerical methods and digital computers in the solution of algebraic, transcendental, simultaneous, ordinary and partial differential equations.

courses.subject: EGGN
courses.title: Professional Practice
courses.description: Professional engineering work in industry or government. Written report required. May be taken for credit for a maximum of three units. Applicable towards bachelor's degree programs. Not for credit in the graduate program.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Global Geography
courses.description: Introduction to world's geographical regions. Cultural patterns and their evolution in diverse physical environments.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Intro to Natural Environment
courses.description: Introduction to the major components of the physical environment, including landforms, climate, natural vegetation and soils.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Introduction to the Natural Environment: Laboratory
courses.description: Observations, experiments and demonstrations designed to familiarize students with techniques utilized by physical geographers. Topics include weather and climate, vegetation, and landforms.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Global Environmental Problems
courses.description: Geographical analysis of the Earth's principal environmental problems. Population growth, agriculture and pesticides, climate change, forestry and fishing, energy, endangered species, and appropriate development.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Human Geography
courses.description: Introduction to Human Geography. Understanding the regional distribution of language, religion, population, migration and settlement patterns, political organization, technology, methods of livelihood over the earth.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Digital Earth: Introduction to Geospatial Technologies
courses.description: Introduction to geospatial technologies, including, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Global Positioning Systems (GPS), remote sensing. Web mapping and location-based services.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Welcome to Geography: Mapping the First Year
courses.description: Introduction to geography as an academic discipline. Research and experiential opportunities available to Geography majors. Develop key skills for academic and professional success. Promote community and student engagement with geography.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Introduction to Spatial Data
courses.description: Introduction to the variety of evidence used in geographic analysis and the sources and techniques for acquiring geographic evidence.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Weather and Climate
courses.description: Atmospheric elements and controls, fronts, severe weather and climatic classification systems.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Cities and Nature
geCategories:
Implications & Explorations in Phys/Bio
Free Course Material
courses.description: Impact of urbanization on landforms, climate, vegetation, and animals. Planning implications and case studies.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: The Global Economy
courses.description: Geographic perspectives on the global production of goods and services and their distribution to consumers. Key geographic issues in uneven development, international trade, investment patterns, and the spatial integration of local and regional economies.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: The National Parks
courses.description: The creation and use of national parks and other protected areas. Origins and globalization of the national parks. Challenges and conflicts related to national parks.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Global Cuisines
courses.description: The geography of food and global cuisines, focusing on origin, diffusion, tradition, change and adaptation.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Geographic Thought
courses.description: Introduction to geographic thought through readings, discussion, and writing assignments. Physical, environmental, regional and spatial traditions in geography, and current themes in geographic research. Meets the upper-division writing requirement for geography majors.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Tropical Rainforests
courses.description: Discussion/seminar examining the geography, ecology and human use of tropical rainforests. Causes and consequences of deforestation, sustainable development and preservation.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Urban Planning Principles
courses.description: Seminar/discussion on conceptual themes and legal foundations of American urban planning. Policy areas associated with urbanization and suburbanization processes: land use, economic development, redevelopment, housing systems, neighborhood dynamics and growth management. (GEOG 478 and POSC 478 are the same course.)

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Geographic Information Systems: Introduction
courses.description: Methods and applications of computer-assisted mapping and geographic information systems. Instructional fee. (2 hours discussion, 3 hours lab)

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Geographic Information Systems: Principles and Applications
courses.description: Integrated computer-assisted methods for handling spatial data, including database design, data conversion and updating, information retrieval, analysis, modeling and mapping. Instructional fee.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Environmental Remote Sensing
courses.description: Fundamentals of remote sensing science and digital image processing. Remote sensing principles and the processing and interpretation of remotely sensed data using image processing techniques and software.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Physical Environment
courses.description: Research in physical and environmental geography: methods and contemporary themes. Case studies in climatology, geomorphology, GIS and plant geography.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Seminar: Selected Topics in Geography
courses.description: Various topics selected from any of the subfields of geography. Chosen topic and general outline of the seminar are circulated prior to registration. May be repeated once with different topic.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Project
courses.description: Requires consent of adviser.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: Requires advancement to candidacy.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: GRMN
courses.title: Fundamental German-A
courses.description: Develop listening and reading comprehension, speaking and cultural awareness to communicate on a basic level. Introduction to customs and culture of German-speaking countries. Conducted primarily in German.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: World Civilizations to the 16th Century
courses.description: Development of Western and non-Western civilizations from their origins to the 16th century.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: World Civilizations Since the 16th Century
courses.description: Development of Western and non-Western civilizations from the 16th century to the present.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: United States to 1877
courses.description: Political, social, economic and cultural development of the United States to 1877. Old World background, rise of the new nation, sectional problems, the Civil War and Reconstruction.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: United States Since 1877
courses.description: U.S. history from the late 19th century to the present. Economic transformation, political reform movements, social, cultural and intellectual changes and the role of the United States in world affairs.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Survey of American History
courses.description: American history from prehistoric times (before 1492) to the present according to chronological time periods. Basic themes that pervade the entire sweep of the nation's history. Satisfies state requirement in U.S. History.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Historical Thinking
courses.description: Nature of history, history of historical thought and history's relationship to the humanities and social sciences. Seminar required of all history majors. History majors must earn at a "C" (2.0) or better.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Historical Writing
courses.description: Research, writing and library usage (including computer-assisted bibliographic searches) as related to history. Meets the classroom portion of the upper-division writing requirement for history majors. Seminar required of all history majors. History majors must earn at least a "C" (2.0) in this course.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The California Experience
courses.description: Seven themes in California studies. Explores the California experience through readings, films and music, and three writing assignments that ask them to research one topic each in the arts/humanities, social sciences and natural sciences in California. (LBST 310 and HIST 310 are the same course.)

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: World War II
courses.description: History of World War II: Films, documentaries, lectures and discussion.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Early Science and Technology
courses.description: Science and technology in the development of human culture, especially the interactions among science, technology and society in ancient Greece and China, medieval and Renaissance Europe, and Islam. (HIST 330 and LBST 330 are the same course).

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Women's Image in American Film
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Images, symbols, visual metaphors and myths as they relate to the image of women. Change in film images will be contrasted with the changing status of women in America. Not available for graduate degree credit.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: World War II Japanese American Evacuation
courses.description: World War II eviction and detention of people of Japanese ancestry in the United States, pivoting on the significance of this experience in the areas of civil and human rights, cross-cultural relations and international affairs. Not available for graduate degree credit. (HIST 382 and ASAM 382 are the same course.)

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: War and Society in Ancient Greece
courses.description: The dynamic relationship between the changing ways in which Archaic (800-500 BCE) and Classical (500-300 BCE) Greek societies were structured, and the ways in which the Greeks organized themselves for and conducted warfare.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Tudor Stuart England
courses.description: England from the accession of Henry VII to the Glorious Revolution. Political, institutional, ecclesiastical and cultural aspects of the period of the Tudors and Stuarts.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: West Africa and the African Diaspora
courses.description: West African relationships with the African diaspora in the Americas. Issues of the origins of political conflict, economic exploitation, racism, gender, revolts and emancipation, Pan-Africanism and rights of African descendants since the 15th century.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Southern Africa in the 20th Century
courses.description: Twentieth-century developments in the Union (Republic) of South Africa, Central Africa (the Rhodesias and Nyasaland) and Portuguese colonies; the political, economic and social ramifications of race relations.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Ancient China
courses.description: Chinese history from ancient times to the middle of the 17th century; society, thought, economy and political institutions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Japan
courses.description: Social, political, and economic history of Japan until 1868, stressing the Tokugawa era.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Modern Vietnam
courses.description: History of Vietnam since 1802. The French colonial experience, the Vietnamese struggle against the French from 1946 to 1954, and the American involvement in Vietnam.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: United States Cultural History
courses.description: Cultural values, ideas and beliefs of American communities as expressed through a variety of media, including historical, literary, visual, material and aural sources.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Senior Seminar in Historiography and Theory
courses.description: Precedes HIST 490T in the same topic. The historiography, methodology and analytical frameworks used in the particular topic's sub-field. Culminates in a research proposal to be used in 490T. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History Internship
courses.description: Offers work experience related to the history academic program or to areas of public and private employment where any liberal arts major is appropriate. May be repeated once for credit.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Open to advanced students in history with consent of department chair. May be repeated once for credit.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Seminar in European History
courses.description: Utilize primary sources in writing research papers on European History. May be repeated once for credit with different sub-field.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Directed Readings Seminar in World and Comparative History
courses.description: Variable topics reading seminar designed to offer a comprehensive background in the literature of world and comparative history. May be repeated once for credit with different topic. Requires 3-unit upper-division course in world history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Seminar in American History
courses.description: Utilize primary sources in writing research papers on American History. May be repeated once for credit with different topic.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Graduate Internship in History
courses.description: Professional-level internship in historical work. Usually precedes HIST 597, Project and constitutes research phase of main graduate exercise, as well as preparation for post-graduate career. May be repeated once for credit. Requires classified graduate status.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History Project
courses.description: Editing a significant body of primary source materials, including a critical and interpretive introduction, as well as appropriate reference and explanatory notes. Foreign sources will normally be translated into English. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Requires consent of department chair.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Introduction to University Honors Colloquium
courses.description: Required of University Honors students. Introduction to the University Honors Program.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Seminar in Critical Thinking
courses.description: Seminar for first-year Honors Program students. Developing critical thinking skills. Interpretation, analysis, criticism and advocacy of ideas encountered in designated Honors Program activities.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Seminar in Oral Communication
courses.description: Seminar for first-year Honors Program students, emphasizing oral communication skills. Construction, presentation and critical analysis of oral presentations related to the ideas encountered in designated Honors Program activities. Instruction in effective oral communication and critical thinking.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Being Scholarly and Creative in an Interdisciplinary World
courses.description: Required of all University Honors students. Interdisciplinary consideration of academic research and creative activities.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Seminar: American Institutions and Values to 1877
courses.description: Critically examines the historical development and political culture of American institutions and values from Colonial history to the Reconstruction era. The interaction, conflict and cooperation of diverse groups, with specific attention to race, ethnicity, gender and class.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Seminar: American Institutions and Values since 1877
courses.description: Critically examines the development of American institutions and values from Reconstruction to present day, with particular reference to California government and politics. The interaction, conflict and cooperation of diverse groups with specific attention to race, ethnicity, gender and class.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Seminar: World Civilizations to 1500
courses.description: Integrative, holistic introductory survey of the historical development of civilization within a global context. Impact of Western institutions and ideas upon non-Western societies and cultures and the influence of non-Western cultures and peoples upon Western societies and cultures.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Proposal Colloquium
courses.description: Prepare proposal for the Senior Honors Project and submit to an appropriate faculty mentor. Required of all University Honors Students.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Seminar in Natural Science and Mathematics
courses.description: Interdisciplinary seminar examining selected topics in natural science and mathematics.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Seminar in Arts and Humanities
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Interdisciplinary seminar examining selected topics in arts and humanities. May be repeated for credit with different topic.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Seminar in Lifelong Learning
courses.description: Interdisciplinary seminar examining selected topics in lifelong learning.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Senior Honors Colloquium
courses.description: Interdisciplinary dialogue, presentation and evaluation of the senior honors project.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Senior Honors Project
courses.description: Supervised individual research or creative activity. Work toward completing an honors project, which is required in order to graduate with University Honors. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Independent Study
courses.description: Study of special topic(s) in consultation with and completed under the supervision of a member of the honors faculty, or other faculty upon approval of the director of the Honors Program. May be repeated for a maximum of 3 units.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Introduction to Human Communication
courses.description: Theory and practice of interpersonal communication. Practice in the development of skills for improving the quality of communication is required.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Public Speaking
courses.description: Theory and presentation of public speeches, including an analysis of determinants of comprehension and attitude formation; selection and organization of speech materials, development of delivery skills and evaluation of message effectiveness. Student presentations required. Participation in research projects.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Interpersonal Conflict Management
courses.description: Nature, causes and structure of interpersonal conflict; communication strategies exhibited in conflict; and intervention principles for conflict management. Conflict management theory is applied to conflicts within marriages, small groups, organizations and intercultural relationships.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Essentials of Argumentation
courses.description: Methods of critical inquiry and advocacy. Identify fallacies in reasoning, testing evidence and evidence sources; advancing a reasoned position; and defend and refute arguments. Analysis and evaluation of oral and written arguments.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Introduction to Research in Speech Communication
courses.description: Understanding and using professional literature in speech communication and using that literature to generate a formal research paper. A passing grade fulfills the course requirement of the university upper division baccalaureate writing requirement for communication studies majors and communicative disorders majors.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Introduction to Communication Theory
courses.description: Theories and competencies in interpersonal, small group, public, organizational and intercultural communication. Variations in communication processes across contexts are investigated.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Introduction to Communication and Critical/Cultural Studies
courses.description: Introduction to critical/cultural studies of communication. Canonical theoretical texts and primary methods and areas of study. Culture and representation as sites of personal, social and cultural identities. Vocabulary and tools applicable to furthering progressive social, economic and political change.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Interpersonal Communication Theory
courses.description: Behavioral and humanistic approaches to theories of interpersonal communication. Functions of communication that influence interpersonal relationships, including communicator characteristics, information exchange, situational demands and interpersonal evaluations.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Intercultural Communication
courses.description: Communication problems that result when members of different cultures communicate. How interpersonal communication can overcome differences in cultures' perceptions of communication's functionality, value orientations, nonverbal behavior, language, epistemologies and rhetorics.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Communicating in Teams and Groups
courses.description: Applying communication theories and behavioral research findings as they relate to small groups and teams. Communication facilitation among individuals in task realization, including interpersonal needs, leadership, norms, roles, verbal and nonverbal messages, and group systems and procedures.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Intercollegiate Forensics
courses.description: Directed activity in debate and other forensic events. Participation in intercollegiate speech competition is required for credit. May be repeated once for credit. (More than 6 hours of class work for each unit of credit.)

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Communication Theory
courses.description: Various theories and perspectives on human communication. Understanding basic forms of theories and developing theoretical perspectives on human communication.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Intergroup Communication
courses.description: This course explores social identity complexity and communication dynamics in different contexts including intergenerational, ethnolinguistic vitality, intercultural, ability-disability, sexual orientation, workplace, health, and sports. Intergroup theories such as social identity theory, cutting-edge studies and media illustrations will inform class discussion.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Communication Studies Capstone
courses.description: Gives advanced students opportunity to integrate and synthesize what they have learned. Prepares them to be competent communicators in their personal, civic and professional roles and is the final class before graduation.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Internship in Communication Studies
courses.description: On-site involvement with communication frameworks as they function in ongoing organizational settings. Working in an organization and seminar activities. Application for internship must be submitted prior to enrollment.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Open to upper-division students in speech communication only with signed consent form from department chair. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Research in Speech Communication
courses.description: Research design and methods used in historical, descriptive and experimental research in speech communication. A "B" (3.0) or better is required for credit in the Communication Studies M.A.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Seminar in Intercultural Communication
courses.description: Theory and methodology in intercultural communication research. Specific variables examined include attribution, values, communication competence and acculturation/adaptation. Practice in completing original research in intercultural communication.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Directed Graduate Research
courses.description: Individual research study, under the supervision of the chair of the student's advisory committee.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: The selection, investigation and written presentation of a selected problem in the field of speech.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: The selection, investigation and written presentation of a selected problem in the field of speech.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: The selection, investigation and written presentation of a selected problem in the field of speech.

courses.subject: HCOM
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: Open to graduate students only with signed consent from department chair. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Introduction to Aging Studies
courses.description: Multidisciplinary overview of: characteristics, strengths and problems of older persons; diversity in aging process involving gender, race, ethnicity, subculture; services to older adults; gerontology as an academic discipline and a field of practice. (AGNG 133, SOCI 133, PUBH 133, HUSR 133 and PSYC 133 are the same course.)

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Introduction to Human Services
courses.description: Origin and scope of human services, including theoretical frameworks, the functions and activities of human services organizations, and the roles and related skills of human services workers.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Case Management
courses.description: Principles and critical issues in case management, along with various models of service delivery. Special attention given to the diverse populations utilizing case management systems. Collaborative and interagency services.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Research and Data Management in Human Services
courses.description: Basic research and assessment skills appropriate to the delivery of human services. Introductory skills relating to library search techniques, evaluation of research articles, computer based data analysis, tracking of client progress and implications for human services.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Leadership Skills and Personal Development
courses.description: Leadership concepts and skills, including psychological process, conflict resolution, counseling and human service skills. Becoming aware of personal leadership styles; maintaining vitality through physical and mental health. (HUSR 350 and COUN 350 are the same course).

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Theories and Techniques of Counseling
courses.description: Contemporary theories and techniques of counseling. The counseling process, comparison of various theoretical approaches, introduction to professional and ethical issues.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Program Design and Proposal Writing
courses.description: Techniques of program design, budgeting and staffing of human service programs; proposal writing and fund development methods; survey of needs assessment procedures.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Practicum Seminar
courses.description: Participation at an approved agency conducting appropriate human service duties. Discussions related to: functions and structures of human services agencies; interrelationships with community services; the role of the human services worker; ethical, legal and professional issues.

sections.instructor: Sapna Chopra, Sapna Chopra, Sapna Chopra, Sapna Chopra
Gary Germo, To Be Announced, To Be Announced, To Be Announced

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Peer Mentoring for HUSR Student Success
courses.description: Develop mentorship skills through seminar learning and serving as a peer mentor to other students. Enhance communication, cultural competency, leadership, motivation, goal achievement, personal management and student success skills. Learn about barriers to and resources for college student success.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Ethical and Professional Issues in Human Services
courses.description: Ethical, legal and professional issues facing the human services worker. Designed to teach a process of ethical decision-making and to increase awareness of the complexities in practice.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Crisis Intervention for Para-Professionals
courses.description: Emphasis on theories and techniques of short-term intervention and referral procedures addressing societal crises including suicide, cultural, developmental, loss, veterans, PTSD, community disaster, IPV, child abuse, sexual assault/rape, sexuality, bullying, substance misuse, gun violence, the pandemic, and social media issues.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Advocacy and Social Change in Communities
courses.description: Provides a framework for understanding the human service needs of diverse and marginalized community groups through the lens of power, privilege, and oppression. Emphasis is placed on developing self-awareness, cultural humility, and advocacy skills.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Treatment Issues in Drug Addiction
courses.description: Treatment issues and theoretical models involved in treating drug dependencies. Specific effects of different drug classifications; understanding drug cultures; women, children and elderly addiction; co-dependency and enabling.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Group Process and Membership
courses.description: Didactic and experiential overview of stages of group development, impact of members on group identity, group member and leader issues. Survey various counseling groups. May be repeated for a maximum of 3 units. Credit/No Credit only.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Contemporary Issues in the Human Services
courses.description: Systematic study and theory, research findings and intervention strategies related to contemporary issues faced by paraprofessional human service workers. May be repeated with different topics for a maximum of 9 units.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Child Abuse and the Human Services
courses.description: Introduction to types and symptoms of abuse, assessment techniques, legal and ethical issues, family dynamics pertaining to children, adolescents and adults abused as children. Networking and referral, utilizing community resources and prevention.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Physiological Effects of Alcohol and Other Drugs
courses.description: Pharmacological actions of drugs of abuse and how these relate to the physiological, psychological and behavioral effects of such drugs. Properties of recreational, "street" drugs and of prescription drugs that lead to abuse and/or dependence are covered. Not available for use on a graduate study plan.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Dynamics of Substance Abuse Treatment in Families
courses.description: Explore and apply methods of assisting significant others, organizations and communities to understand, treat and prevent substance abuse and dependence. Students develop practice strategies that will prepare them to deliver services at the micro, meso and macro levels. Not available for use on a graduate study plan.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Evaluation of Human Services Programs
courses.description: Making program objectives measurable; determining appropriate methodology and techniques to evaluate effectiveness, efficiency and process variables; practical problems of program evaluation.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Fieldwork Seminar
courses.description: Students participate in 120 hours of service at an approved agency, 8 hours per week. Classroom analysis of agency experience focusing on skills and techniques of human service workers and organizational analysis.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Internship Seminar
courses.description: Supervised internship in a community service agency in area of specialization. Seminar consists of group supervision and discussion of cases. Letter grade only. Internship experience consisting of 120 hours with a minimum of 8 hours per week during the semester.

courses.subject: HUSR
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individual research project, either library or field, under the direction of a faculty member. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units; only three units in one semester. Requires approval of coordinator, consent of instructor.

courses.subject: HSS
courses.title: Careers in Humanities and Social Sciences: Passage to the Future
courses.description: Core values and skills of the humanities and social sciences as they relate to a variety of different professions. Reflect on personal strengths and passions, how they align with different careers and how they lead to meaningful professions.

courses.subject: HSS
courses.title: Humanities Internship
courses.description: Supervised internship requiring course project and 120 hours (3 units) or 240 hours (6 units).

courses.subject: HSS
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent research project in humanities or social sciences. May be repeated once for credit with different content. No more than three units may be taken in any one semester.

courses.subject: HSS
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: May be repeated once for credit with different content. No more than three units may be taken in any one semester. Requires consent of home department graduate advisor.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Principles of Business Data Analytics
courses.description: Statistical data analysis and inference techniques within the context of business analytics. Selecting statistical tools that are appropriate for a given application. Use Microsoft Excel to analyze data.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Introduction to Programming
courses.description: Introduction to fundamental Object Oriented Programming concepts, including variables, control structures, functions, object-oriented principles and data handling; preparing for advanced programming and data analytics.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Business Analytics
courses.description: Advanced concepts and applications of business analytics. Developing analytical thinking, applying business analytics solutions, and communicating insights based on the solutions to decision makers in an organization.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Principles of Information Systems
courses.description: How business professionals can leverage Information Systems (IS) through planning, oversight and management. Understanding the implications of IS, learning to identify and evaluate potential opportunities to employ IS, understanding the role of IS as a major facilitator of the fundamental business activities and learning to manage IS projects.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Systems Analysis and Design
courses.description: Systems analysis and design for business information systems; systems development methodologies; managing changes to system parameters; systems process and data models; case tool types and their use; structured vs. object oriented analysis and design.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Business Telecommunications for Information System Design
courses.description: Essential concepts for developing a data communication architecture to support information systems for a business enterprise. Requires group project to design a LAN.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Business Applications using Web Technologies
courses.description: Contemporary issues in the design and development of integrated, graphical user interface-based business applications.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Principles of Business Intelligence
courses.description: Principles and procedures related to the design and use of expert systems and decision support systems principles in management decision making; development of expert systems using shells.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Privacy and Security
courses.description: Security and privacy problems associated with the use of computer systems; ways to minimize risks and losses.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Integrated Enterprise Information Systems
courses.description: Application programming fundamentals for ERP systems; accessing and management of ERP database tables and external files; layout design and data extraction for advanced output; testing, debugging and analysis tools; security issues in an ERP system.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Business Modeling Using Spreadsheets
courses.description: Spreadsheet-based business decision modeling emphasizing model formulation, optimization and applications, including resource allocation, scheduling, capital budgeting, facility location, queueing, Markov chains and simulation to analyze uncertainty. Build and interpret models to support data-driven decisions.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Senior Project: Information Systems Development
courses.description: Integrates information systems development concepts of analysis, design and implementation. Develop an information system from concept to completion. Individual and team effort.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Data Mining for Managers
courses.description: Fundamentals of data mining. Topics may include association, classification, clustering, decision trees, statistical modeling, and visualization. Motivation for the applications of data mining techniques. Use of data mining software suites on data sets.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Applied Business Forecasting
courses.description: Forecasting methods applied to problems in business and industry; practical multiple regression models with computer solutions; basic techniques in time-series analysis of trend, cyclical and seasonal components; correlation of time-series and forecasting with the computer.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: Planned and supervised work experience. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Credit/No Credit or 3-unit Letter Grade option. Only 3-unit Letter Grade option will fulfill practicum requirement. Consent of department internship adviser needed.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Open to qualified students desiring to pursue directed independent inquiry. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Not open to students on academic probation. Requires approval by the Department Chair.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Statistics for Data Science
courses.description: Quantitative analysis and data visualization in R programming, random variables and probability distributions, sampling distributions, confidence intervals and testing hypotheses, p-value and significance level, regression analysis to measure relationships and ANOVA to analyze designed experiments.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Decision Models for Business and Economics
courses.description: Linear programming; inventory; PERT-CPM; queuing; computer simulation; time-series forecasting; and other optional topics.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Data Mining for Business Applications
courses.description: Fundamentals of data mining. Association, classification, clustering, decision trees, statistical modeling and visualization. Motivation for the applications of data mining techniques. Introduction to business analytics and case studies. Use of data mining software suites on data sets.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Forecasting for Analytical Decision Making
courses.description: Blend classical and modern forecasting (machine learning) methods. Quantify uncertainty, evaluate models and link forecasts to strategic decisions. Applications span finance, operations, marketing, technology and public policy.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Marketing Analytics for Managers
courses.description: Organizations are increasingly becoming data-driven and are actively seeking managers with knowledge and experience in data analysis and marketing analytics. Focuses on the integrative application of various marketing analytics techniques to solve typical business problems. (ISDS 543 and MKTG 543 are the same course).

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Enterprise Networks
courses.description: Develop data communication architecture for a business enterprise. Concepts of cloud computing, IP-based communications, internetworking and protocol layers. Network infrastructure, operations and management, and security. Technical implications of conducting business on the Internet.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Info Resources and IT Project Management
courses.description: Organizational information resources and IT project management principles, emphasizing strategic use of information resources, and methodologies and practice of project management through hands-on exercises and real-world group projects.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Cybersecurity for Business
courses.description: Organizational and technological issues of cybersecurity, including cyber threats against enterprises and methods of protecting assets from threats. Operational, managerial and technical countermeasures utilized by organizations to safeguard confidentiality, integrity and availability.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Advanced Regression Analysis for Business Applications
courses.description: Apply regression to develop prediction models for a variety of business decision problems using real case studies and examples. Data issues, appropriate use of statistical software, and various aspects and extensions of linear regression models for different data types.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Business Data Transformation
courses.description: ETL/ELT aspects of business data analysis. Relational and multidimensional data extraction from local and remote sources, designing ETL processes, querying multidimensional cubes, dimension and time-based hierarchies, and adding calculated members.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Seminar in Information Systems Implementation
courses.description: Integrates the development concepts of project management, analysis, design and implementation with telecommunications, database design, programming, testing and system integration issues.
