Develop information systems from concept to completion through individual and team effort. Requires projects. Individual project will fulfill the terminal degree requirement. To be taken in the last semester or with completion of at least seven ISDS courses in the program.

courses.subject: ISDS
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Not open to students on academic probation. Requires consent of department chair and associate dean.

courses.subject: IDT
courses.title: Emerging Technologies for Learning
courses.description: This course will focus on the use and theoretical basis of a variety of emerging technologies for learning. Introduces trends and issues in emerging technologies, online teaching, usability and accessibility, and lesson plan design utilizing technology.

courses.subject: IDT
courses.title: Foundations of Instructional Design and Digital Authoring Tools
courses.description: Understanding operating systems, hardware and networking environments to develop instructional tools and products using a multimedia authoring tool.

courses.subject: IDT
courses.title: Research Practices in Instructional Design and Technology
courses.description: Terms and accepted procedures in qualitative and quantitative inquiry as they apply to instructional design and technology. Conduct controlled portions of IDT research and prepare preliminary proposals for larger projects. Requires completion of orientation program for M.S. in Instructional Design and Technology (IDT).

courses.subject: IDT
courses.title: Systematic Approaches to Digital Design and Development
courses.description: Design, develop and implement digital media for instructional purposes. Issues surrounding using digital media for instruction. Requires successfully completing Midpoint Symposium.

courses.subject: IDT
courses.title: Trends, Emerging Technologies and Issues in Instructional Design
courses.description: Theoretical basis, issues and strategies for improving teaching and learning through the use of emerging technologies.

courses.subject: IS
courses.title: International Studies
courses.description: May be taken for credit for a maximum of twelve units.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Fundamental Italian-A
courses.description: Develop listening and reading comprehension, speaking and writing, and cultural awareness to communicate on a basic level with a focus on oral expression. Introduction to Italian customs, culture and civilization. Conducted primarily in Italian.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Fundamental Japanese-A
courses.description: Develop listening and reading comprehension, speaking, writing, and cultural awareness to communicate on a basic level in Japanese. Introduction to Japanese customs, culture and civilization.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Fundamental Japanese-B
courses.description: Continued development of listening and reading comprehension, speaking, writing, and cultural awareness to communicate on a basic level in Japanese. Further study of Japanese customs, culture and civilization.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Intermediate Japanese-A
courses.description: Develop listening and reading comprehension, and oral and written proficiency in Japanese based on cultural and literary materials. Review and introduce grammar. Conducted primarily in Japanese.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Japanese Cultural Conversation and Composition A
courses.description: Subjects related to Japanese culture. Helps develop Japanese oral and written proficiency through discussions, oral and written reviews, and essays. Conducted primarily in Japanese.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Advanced Japanese-A
courses.description: Practice in four skills of advanced Japanese, emphasizing reading comprehension in the context of contemporary concerns. Conducted in Japanese.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Introduction to Japanese Civilization
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Readings and lectures in Japanese literature, arts and institutions from earliest history to 1868, to develop insights into Japanese culture while strengthening facility in the language. Conducted primarily in Japanese.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Japanese Culture and Society: Anime
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Japanese culture and society, as well as multicultural analysis of global issues as reflected in Japanese animated films. Conducted in English.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Japanese Culture and Society in Film
courses.description: Development of modern Japanese culture and society using film that reflects important Japanese cultural and social concepts, and ways of looking at and dealing with the world. Conducted primarily in Japanese.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Japanese Language and Society
courses.description: Introduces the methodology for analyzing the Japanese language in its social dimension. Major dialectal areas in Japan and their linguistic characteristics, social class and language, and language and gender. Conducted primarily in Japanese.

courses.subject: KORE
courses.title: Korean Culture and Society: K-Pop
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Korean culture and society, as well as multicultural analysis of global issues, as reflected in Korean popular music. Examines K-pop as both text and industry. Conducted in English.

courses.subject: LBST
courses.title: Introduction to the Humanities
courses.description: Interdisciplinary introduction to the humanities as a set of related disciplines that apply conceptual, critical, historical and linguistic analyses to advance our understanding of what it means to be human.

courses.subject: LBST
courses.title: Introduction to the Social Sciences
courses.description: Major topics in the social sciences in order to understand their systematic study of human behavior, to realize the connections among particular issues and approaches, and to reflect critically on modern life.

courses.subject: LBST
courses.title: Historical Dimension of Liberal Studies
courses.description: Origins and development of modes of thought and forms of expression in the three core areas of liberal studies, i.e., the natural sciences, social sciences, and arts and humanities.

courses.subject: LBST
courses.title: Historical Dimension of Liberal Studies
courses.description: Origins and development of modes of thought and forms of expression in the three core areas of liberal studies, i.e., the natural sciences, social sciences, and arts and humanities.

courses.subject: LBST
courses.title: Liberal Studies in the Humanities and Arts
courses.description: Interdisciplinary approach to the humanities and arts that examines their purposes, structures and major developments since 1900.

courses.subject: LBST
courses.title: Liberal Studies in the Sciences
courses.description: Interdisciplinary introduction to the character and aims of 20th-century science, current theories and knowledge, and the role of science and technology in contemporary society.

courses.subject: LBST
courses.title: Liberal Studies in the Social Sciences
courses.description: Interdisciplinary introduction to modern social science in which major thinkers, ideas, movements and problems will be approached historically, comparatively and analytically.

courses.subject: LBST
courses.title: Food in the Social Sciences
courses.description: Interdisciplinary exploration of the study of food in the social sciences. The meanings of food in the construction of society and culture across time and space.

courses.subject: LBST
courses.title: Ancient Eats: Food and Foodways in the Ancient World
geCategories: Explorations in the Arts or Humanities
courses.description: Food in the Roman Empire and elsewhere in the ancient world. Farming, sustainability, trade, purchasing, processing, production, ingredients, terroir, recipes, tools, the place and function of feasts, and food in myth, cult and philosophy (LBST 341 and HIST 341 are the same course.)

courses.subject: LBST
courses.title: Senior Seminar in Great Books
courses.description: Important books from early civilization to the present. Develops critical reading of texts, clear expression of ideas and integration of knowledge. Student-led discussions.

courses.subject: LBST
courses.title: Internship in Liberal Studies
courses.description: Learning experience for undergraduates at any public or private institution to which a Liberal Studies major/minor or Food Studies minor is related. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: LBST
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individually supervised studies and/or projects. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Department consent and approval by the Liberal Studies department chair required.

courses.subject: LIBR
courses.title: Library Research Center Internship
courses.description: Peer-led research services at the Pollak Library. Learn directly from librarians, engage in reflective writing, explore information science concepts and work collaboratively with peers in person at the Research Center desk.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language and Linguistics
courses.description: Nature of language, its origin and development; language in culture, the structure of language and its systems of writing and transcription, and its application to other areas of humanistic and scientific knowledge.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: The English Language in America
courses.description: American English, its origins, regional and social dialects and role in American history and in such institutions as schools, corporations, government and media.  Requirement for application to English Teaching Credential. (ENGL 305 and LING 305 are the same course.)

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Linguistic Phonetics and Phonology
courses.description: Nature and structure of sound systems in language. Thorough investigation of the International Phonetic Alphabet as applied to many different languages including English. Language Acquisition (L1) and Language Learning (L2); analytic methods and techniques.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Sociolinguistics
courses.description: Social dialects in relation to the surrounding communities. Social stratification, acculturation, language maintenance, standardization, language planning and language change.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Psycholinguistics
courses.description: Theory and research on the psychological processes that make possible language acquisition and written language; speech production; and language acquisition. (PSYC 417 and LING 417 are the same course.)

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language, Gender, Identity and Social Bias
courses.description: How gender, gender-intersecting identities, and social attitudes and biases are reflected in the structure and use of language; gender in language: does linguistic behavior influence thought?

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Research Methods and Bibliography
courses.description: Principal books, periodicals and collections in general linguistics, specific languages and related fields; techniques of preparing research papers and field reports in linguistics. Must be taken prior to LING 597.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Phonological Analysis
courses.description: Phonological systems that occur in languages; emphasizes terminology used to describe changes in the system and processes affecting it; problem solving of selected language date.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Project
courses.description: Preparation and completion of an approved project

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Business and Its Legal Environment
courses.description: Federal, state and international laws and ethical issues affecting business, including the legal system, litigation and alternative dispute resolution, the Constitution, torts, criminal law, contracts, various forms of business organizations, employment laws and discrimination, and consumer and environmental protection.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Managing Operations
courses.description: Integrates selected general management concepts with operations management concepts and techniques. Emphasizes the development of competencies required for effective planning, designing, operating, controlling and improving processes that produce and deliver quality goods and services.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Organizational Behavior
courses.description: Individual, group and organizational influences on human behavior in organizations. Topics include personality and emotions, motivation, decision-making, group and team effectiveness, leadership, power and politics, organizational culture and change.

sections.instructor: Edward De La Torre, Edward De La Torre, Edward De La Torre, Edward De La Torre, Edward De La Torre, Edward De La Torre, Edward De La Torre, Edward De La Torre, Edward De La Torre

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Human Resource Management
courses.description: Human resource management functions in organizations. Topics include selection, recruiting, training, compensation and performance appraisal.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: International Law for Business
courses.description: International laws and ethical issues affecting businesses including: the WTO and UN; international agreements, treaties and regional organizations (e.g., EU, NAFTA); international contracts; and national and international regulation of imports, exports and competition.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Commercial Law
courses.description: Philosophy, institutions and role of law and ethical considerations in commercial transactions. Case studies in sales, storage and shipment of goods, commercial paper, debtor and creditor rights and remedies, bankruptcy, secured transactions and suretyship.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Law for Small Business
courses.description: Federal and state laws and ethical issues affecting small businesses (e.g., sole proprietorships), including litigation involving negligence, product liability, discrimination, consumer protection and workers' compensation claims.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: International Business and Management
courses.description: Fundamental course in international business and international management. Overview of international business, and emphasizes a managerial approach that involves examining the various roles of managers in an international setting.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Entertainment Business
courses.description: Business and management aspects of media-based (film, television, etc.) and ground-based (live theater, sports, etc.) entertainment enterprises.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Operations Planning and Control
courses.description: Analytical approach to explore planning and scheduling material, capital and human resources to meet customer demand. Topics include master scheduling, material requirements planning/ERP, production activity control, inventory management, warehouse management and physical distribution.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Purchasing and Supply Management
courses.description: Operational and strategic role of purchasing/supply management in organizations. Develops skills and knowledge in supplier selection/evaluation, negotiation, cost/price analysis, contract management, global sourcing, commodity analysis, value analysis. Exercises, cases, guest speakers.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Quality Management
courses.description: Measurement and improvement of productivity and quality in organizations. Problem-solving and process management tools. Case analyses and research projects address issues of people and technology. How to improve your organization: manufacturing or service, department or company.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Supply Chain Management
courses.description: Managing materials, capital and information flows throughout multiple organizations in a supply chain from acquisition of materials to delivery of finished goods and services to the final customers. Presentation and case studies on various issues in supply chain management.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Charting the Future of Work
courses.description: Opportunities and pitfalls facing 21st-century organizations. Topics include the historical context and evolution of work, transformative technologies, and justice, equity, diversity and inclusion.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Staffing
courses.description: Theories and techniques related to employee staffing. Topics include the planning, legal issues, job analysis, measurement, internal and external recruitment and selection, and decision-making.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Compensation
courses.description: Developing equitable compensation and benefit programs in order to retain a productive workforce. Topics include job analysis and evaluation, pay structures, salary survey, individual compensation, incentive systems and benefits.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Management of Service Organizations
courses.description: Develop skills to successfully manage service businesses. Topics include managing service firms through integration with operations, strategy, marketing, technology and organizational issues. Provides theory, tools and experiential insight into how these aspects can be successfully used in a service-oriented business.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Training and Development
courses.description: Theoretical and practical issues involved in designing and implementing training and development programs in work organizations. Topics include planning, designing and delivering training interventions, and evaluating training effectiveness.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Business and Society
courses.description: Open to nonbusiness majors. Analyze and interpret real-world interrelationships between firms and their external environments. Contemporary and emerging trends in areas, such as technology, politics, economics, natural environment, business ethics and other societal aspects.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Team Leadership Skills
courses.description: Interpersonal skills required to lead teams effectively. Topics include self-awareness, managing stress, creative problem-solving, communicating supportively, effective use of power and influence, motivating others, managing conflict, empowering employees, building effective teams, leading positive change.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Project Management
courses.description: Principles and techniques of effective project management. Managerial, organizational and behavioral concepts, as well as effective tools, techniques and software for planning, communications, coordination and control of the project.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Employment Law
courses.description: Federal and state laws, and ethical issues affecting employment relationships and discrimination. Topics include the laws of agency and employees, independent contractors, the hiring process and procedures, wages, hours, benefits, termination of employment, OSHA and workers' compensation.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Entertainment Business Law
courses.description: Overview of entertainment industry legal issues in media, publishing, recording and hospitality enterprises. Topics include intellectual property, contracts, labor union representation and government regulation.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Seminar in Strategic Management
courses.description: Integrative cases from top management viewpoint. Analyze the firm's internal and external environment. Formulate strategic decisions to develop and sustain competitive advantage. Implement strategic decisions, organization design and control.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Lean Startup Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Theory and techniques of lean startup entrepreneurship, including customer development, product-market fit and go-to-market strategy. Applies lean startup techniques potentially in consultation with actual startup firms.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Entrepreneurial Management
courses.description: How to plan, organize and control new ventures. Setting up business-level strategy and corresponding systems to improve venture performance. Casework, research and fieldwork with selected local businesses.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Entrepreneurial Leadership
courses.description: Leadership roles, organizational development and human resource management of new ventures. Determining the policies, procedures and culture needed to facilitate employee productivity and effectiveness. May include casework, research and/or fieldwork with selected local businesses.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Entertainment Operations
courses.description: Applies management theories to media-oriented entertainment industries, including film and its ancillary markets (home entertainment, television, streaming, cable), music and video games, among others.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Hospitality and Tourism Management
courses.description: Provides skills and tools for managing business processes, operations and resources in different areas of the hospitality industry (e.g., lodging, theme parks, casinos, special event management).

Ellen E.K. Kim, Ellen E.K. Kim

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Music Business
courses.description: All aspects of the music business, including music business revenue streams, artist management, music marketing, data analytics in the music business, record deals, songwriting royalties, music publishing, music copyright, music supervision, and emerging trends in the music industry.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Global Strategic Management
courses.description: Conceptualization, formulation and implementation of successful global business strategies. Managing cultural differences, strategic alliances and acquisitions in the global market space.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: Planned and supervised internship experience. Requires that: student obtains an internship; internship site and position has met CICE approval; consent of academic department. Letter grade or credit/no credit options available. Only 3-unit letter grade option will fulfill practicum requirement. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Open to qualified students desiring to pursue directed independent inquiry. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Not open to students on academic probation. Requires approval by department chair.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Operations Management
courses.description: Role of operations function in designing, producing and delivering products and services in manufacturing and service firms. Includes strategy and processes to meet market needs, internal and external coordination in a supply chain, long- and short-term decision-making tools and techniques.

sections.instructor: James Lake, James Lake, James Lake, James Lake, James Lake, James Lake, James Lake, James Lake, James Lake

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Seminar in Organizational Behavior
courses.description: Understanding and predicting human behavior to enhance individual, team and organizational performance. Applying effective principles of motivation, team building, influence, leadership and conflict management.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Seminar in Team Leadership Skills
courses.description: Graduate seminar to develop hands-on skills to lead high-performance work teams. Topics include self-awareness, stress management, valuing diversity, supportive communication, creative problem solving, influence and leadership, motivating others, managing conflict, empowering and building effective teams.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Supply Chain Management
courses.description: Effective supply chain strategies emphasizing how to plan and integrate supply chain components into a coordinated system. Concepts and models important in supply chain planning. Risk pooling and inventory placement, integrated planning and collaboration and information sharing. Various models and methods for supply chain analysis and optimization.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Leadership Dynamics
courses.description: Dynamics of effective leadership in organizations. Major principles and practices driving the leadership field.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Leading Organizational Change
courses.description: Develop executive-level capabilities to lead, manage and implement organizational change. Build change leadership skills through exposure to a variety of industries, organizations and decision-making scenarios.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Negotiation
courses.description: Builds on knowledge of individual behavior and social perception with a key focus on integrative bargaining strategies and tactics. Aims to help argue for goals more persuasively, while also enriching others' goals.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Leadership, Power and Influence
courses.description: Socio-economic approaches to leadership. Organizational influence processes, power, and politics in organizations and communities.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Not open to students on academic probation. Requires consent of instructor, department chair and associate dean.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Professional Selling
courses.description: Steps of the sales cycle as an interpersonal influence process. Selling skills and techniques based on communication and buyer behavior concepts. Written sales projects and oral presentations are expected.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Principles of Marketing
courses.description: Applying current theories and concepts in effectively marketing goods and services to define target customers from a domestic and global perspective. Includes market research, identifying target customers, developing product offers, branding, pricing, marketing communications and distribution channels.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Marketing Information Technology
courses.description: Information sources, databases and tools applied by marketers to transform data into useful formats for the strategic decision-making process. Includes segmentation, target marketing and positioning, media selection, market share, break-even analysis, pricing, sales forecasting and profit scenario analysis.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Consumer Behavior
courses.description: Consumer buying patterns, motivation and search behavior. Consumer decision-making process. Inter-disciplinary concepts from economics, sociology, psychology, cultural anthropology and mass communications. Case analyses and research projects.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Marketing Research Methods
courses.description: Marketing research process. Problem formulation, identifying data sources, data collection, analysis techniques, preparing research reports and application of these concepts to marketing research projects.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Managing the Sales Force
courses.description: Sales manager's role in organizing and deploying a field sales force, developing effective sales training programs, designing complete motivation and compensation plans, asserting strong leadership and evaluating sales people's performance. Relies heavily on case studies and group discussion.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Retail Marketing Strategy
courses.description: Evolution of retailing into global, high technology industry; developing integrated marketing and financial strategies. Positioning retail offers to establish and maintain relationships with target customers. Evolving market conditions, buying behavior, retail venues, channel relationships, information, communication and decision support systems, merchandise management.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Sales and Consumer Product Strategies
courses.description: Theories, concepts and current professional practices of sales strategy, retail distribution, strategic marketing and category management based on analyzing customer purchasing behavior and sales data.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Marketing Analytics: Decision Making in the Information Age
courses.description: Applying analysis and modeling techniques to a broad range of marketing decision making domains. (MKTG 443 and ISDS 443 are the same course.)

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Social Media Marketing
courses.description: Concepts and practical skills used by organizations to develop social media marketing strategies. Create social media content (Instagram, Facebook, etc.) and produce actionable analytics from the social media content. (MKTG 444 and ISDS 444 are the same course.)

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Global Marketing
courses.description: Theories of international trade and role of marketing decisions across national boundaries and markets. Concepts and principles of marketing strategies in organizations: recognition of environmental differences; market assessments; entry alternatives; positions of global independence; marketing problems; and critical implications.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Visual Marketing
courses.description: Develop marketing communications through image creation tools, such as Adobe Photoshop, Prezi, Adobe Premiere, Apple iMovie, and Google Sketch Up.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Marketing for Entrepreneurs
courses.description: Covering market analysis for new products and services, competitive analysis, alternatives for entering markets, associated costs and launch feasibility. Casework, research and fieldwork with selected local businesses.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Managing Services Marketing
courses.description: Unique marketing needs and challenges faced by service firms in an increasingly challenging global environment. Strategies for marketing services in a variety of industries: entertainment, tourism, hospitality, health care, financial services. Strategies used by manufacturing firms using service as a competitive strategy.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: A.I. in Marketing: The Next Frontier
courses.description: How A.I. is revolutionizing the marketing landscape, from advertising and analytics to customer service and sales. Use practical insights and case studies to illustrate A.I.-driven marketing techniques; preparing students to navigate the evolving marketing ecosystem.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Multicultural Marketing
courses.description: Multicultural marketing is a discipline that recognizes divergent influences in a varied population and creates customized marketing programs that reach various audiences. Students gain an understanding of the dynamics in a diverse market environment while identifying target audiences and appropriate marketing strategies.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Developing Marketing Strategies
courses.description: Developing marketing strategies involving products as well as services. Case analysis and group interaction. Students will finalize and present portfolio of projects and internships completed over the duration of marketing program.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: Planned and supervised internship experience. Requires that: student obtains an internship; internship site and position meet CICE approval; consent of academic department. Letter grade or credit/no credit options available. Only 3-unit letter grade option will fulfill practicum requirement. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Open to undergraduate students desiring to pursue directed independent inquiry. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Not open to students on academic probation. Requires approval by Department Chair.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Marketing Management
courses.description: Key marketing concepts and their applications to marketing research, segmentation, selecting target markets, product development, pricing, promotion and distribution. Develops senior-level executive decision-making skills from global, ethical and socially responsible perspectives. Requires understanding and application in a major project.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Product and Brand Management
courses.description: How to develop products and brands that deliver value to consumers using qualitative and metric approaches.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Contemporary Topics in Marketing
courses.description: Frameworks and practices for the 21st-century U.S. marketer. How to develop brand strategy and drive competitive advantage in an increasingly diverse marketplace through case studies, discussions and guest speakers.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Independent Graduate Research
courses.description: May be repeated for a maximum of 6 units. Not open to students on academic probation. Requires consent of instructor, department chair and associate dean.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: Social Work Perspectives on Human Behavior II
courses.description: Ecological model used in the social work profession for clinical and policy oriented assessments of human functioning and needs from young adulthood through old age. Reciprocal relationships between human behavior and the social environment.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: Social Work Perspectives on Human Behavior III
courses.description: Social work theory and application regarding development of human psychopathology across the life span, including understanding and diagnosing dysfunctional behaviors with the DSM-5.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: Social Work Practice I
courses.description: Social work roles and integration of those roles within a person-environment perspective. Focuses on an integrative framework combining direct practice with individuals, families, groups and communities with a commitment to organizational and social change.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: Community Mental Health: Advanced Practice I
courses.description: Applying theory and practice with diverse populations utilizing a multicultural framework and case materials to analyze treatment issues and empowerment strategies in community mental health. Individual, family and group strategies.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: Aging: A Multigenerational Perspective: Advanced Social Work Practice
courses.description: Social work practice with older adults from a multigenerational perspective. Biopsychosocial aspects of aging, and effectively assessing the needs of older adult clients and their families.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: Social Welfare Policy and Services I
courses.description: History of social welfare and the social work profession, the evolution of social work values and ethics, and a broad array of U.S. social welfare services including income maintenance, health care, mental health and child welfare.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: Child Welfare Policy and Social Work
courses.description: Conceptual and pragmatic underpinnings of federal, state and local policies, as well as specific laws and regulations influencing social work practice with children, youth and their caregivers.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: Aging, A Multi-Generational Perspective: Policy and Social Work
courses.description: Social policies affecting older adults and their families in relation to political, social, economic and cultural factors. Uses a policy-practice framework to provide a conceptual foundation for possible alternatives to aging and family policy choices.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: Social Work Practicum Instruction I
courses.description: Practicum experience in a social services agency under the supervision of professional social workers. Introduction to the range of professional roles, social services infrastructure and policies, professional ethical standards, case management principles and social work intervention modalities. Requires a minimum of 16 hours per week, for a total of 250 hours, for the semester. Credit/No Credit only.A minimum of 16 hours per week, for a total of 250 hours, is required for the semester. Credit/No Credit grade option only.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: Advanced Social Work Field Instruction I
courses.description: Advanced supervised social work practice in a community agency with a focus on the range of professional social work roles in child welfare or community mental health settings. Requires 2-3 hrs/wk seminar and 16-20 hrs/wk agency placement.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: Social Work Practice with Diverse Populations
courses.description: Prepares future social workers to examine social work case management issues related to disadvantaged client groups based on race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, age and disability status. Ecological diversity-sensitive practice, advocacy and empowerment of vulnerable clients.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: Social Work Practice in School Settings
courses.description: Introduction to social work practice in school settings. The roles of social workers in schools, including organizational and clinical consultation, advocacy, program development and evaluation, liaison functions with families and communities, and direct practice.

courses.subject: MSW
courses.title: MSW Master's Project Development
courses.description: Under direction and approval of a faculty advisor, a student develops and prepares the beginning chapters of their MSW project and submits human subjects' approval to conduct research. Prepares students to complete their project.
